# Plannotator **⭐️ NEW:** [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants. Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw). **It plugs directly into your agent** through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab. For a big change, start a [guided review](https://plannotator.ai/code-review#guided-review): an agent sorts the diff into chapters, the most important first.
## Plannotator Inbox

Watch the demo · More on the Inbox · Docs

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. Any other agent reaches it over MCP with `plannotator inbox mcp`, and `plannotator inbox --help` is the guide an agent reads. ## Herdr Annotate: Plannotator in the Terminal

  

[Herdr Annotate](https://github.com/plannotator/herdr-annotate) brings Plannotator-style review to the terminal: annotate terminal text, review whole Markdown documents and your coding agent's replies inside [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), and send the feedback straight back to the agent as its next message. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Droid replies. Annotations are saved in the Plannotator data directory, so terminal reviews and app reviews compound. ``` herdr plugin install plannotator/herdr-annotate ``` Prefer it standalone? [Plannotator TUI](https://github.com/plannotator/plannotator-tui) powers the document review and runs without Herdr: `brew install plannotator/tap/plannotator-tui`. ## HTML artifacts, live sites, and guided reviews
### Annotate HTML artifacts and live sites Annotate rendered HTML files, or any site running on your machine. A local address opens your app live through a local proxy: you comment on the real page, and hot reload keeps working. `plannotator annotate http://localhost:5173`
### Guided reviews In code review, press **Guide** (or `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G`) and an agent sorts the diff into chapters: the heart of the change first, then its effects, then the glue. Each chapter puts a short overview next to the real diff. Comments you leave there go back to the agent with the rest of your review. [More on guided reviews](https://plannotator.ai/code-review#guided-review)
--- ## Commands On Codex, swap the slash commands for `!plannotator …` (e.g. `!plannotator review`) or the `$plannotator-*` skills. ### Annotate ``` /plannotator-annotate README.md # Local markdown file /plannotator-annotate src/ # Browse and annotate files in a folder /plannotator-annotate https://docs.rs/… # Fetch and annotate any URL /plannotator-annotate report.html --render-html # Render HTML as-is instead of converting /plannotator-last # Annotate the agent's last message ``` Need a realistic document to try? Copy the [product requirements document template and filled example](https://docs.plannotator.ai/templates/product-requirements-document) as Markdown. ### Code review ``` /plannotator-review # Review uncommitted changes /plannotator-review # Review a GitHub pull request /plannotator-review # Review a GitLab merge request plannotator review --gitbutler # Review an active GitButler workspace plannotator review --patch-file reading.diff # Review a static caller-supplied unified diff ``` GitButler users can review the whole workspace, one stack, or one branch layer. See the [GitButler workflow guide](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/gitbutler). ### Plan mode No command needed. Plan mode is wired in through each harness's hooks. Any time your agent creates a plan, the markdown review surface opens for you. ### CLI ``` plannotator sessions # List active Plannotator sessions plannotator sessions --open 1 # Reopen a session in the browser plannotator archive # Browse saved plan decisions read-only ``` --- ## AI built in Ask AI about anything you're reviewing, or launch AI reviews that post comments to the diff. --- ## Sharing Send a plan as a link. A teammate annotates it, and you import their feedback for your agent. Small shares live in the link itself. Large ones are encrypted before upload and expire after 7 days. Anyone with the full link can read it. Turn sharing off with `PLANNOTATOR_SHARE=disabled`. [How sharing works](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/sharing)

For teams: join the Workspaces waitlist

--- ## Install One installer covers almost every agent. It installs the `plannotator` binary, auto-detects your installed agents, and configures hooks, skills, and slash commands for each: ```bash # macOS / Linux / WSL curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows PowerShell irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer downloads the binary from GitHub Releases. A full install can also contact GitHub for release resolution and agent files, and npm for Pi, selected extra skills, or the managed agent-terminal runtime. Pinning `--version` skips only GitHub API release resolution, not the release download. See the [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) for the complete network boundaries. Want just the binary and nothing else? Pass `--minimal` (or export `PLANNOTATOR_MINIMAL=1`) to install only the `plannotator` binary to `~/.local/bin`, skipping every skill, hook, slash command, and per-agent config: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --minimal ``` Then finish the step for your agent: | Agent | After the installer | Details | |---|---|---| | **Amp** | Copy [`plannotator.ts`](apps/amp-plugin/plannotator.ts) into `~/.config/amp/plugins/`, then `plugins: reload`. Workflows live in the command palette. | [README](apps/amp-plugin/README.md) | | **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Restart Claude Code. | [README](apps/hook/README.md) | | **Codex** | Nothing. Plan review is enabled automatically via Codex's experimental `Stop` hook (macOS/Linux/WSL; on native Windows, Codex hooks are experimental and the installer prints manual setup steps). `$plannotator-review`, `$plannotator-annotate`, and `$plannotator-last` skills included. | [README](apps/codex/README.md) | | **Copilot CLI** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator-copilot@plannotator`. Restart. Plan review activates in plan mode (`Shift+Tab`). | [README](apps/copilot/README.md) | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Add `@plannotator/dsh` on DSH's Plugins page, or run `dsh plugin --profile add @plannotator/dsh`. Plan review opens on `exit_plan_mode`. The plugin adds `/plannotator-review`, `/plannotator-annotate` and `/plannotator-last`, which open without blocking the session. | [README](apps/dsh-plugin/README.md) | | **Droid** | `droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/backnotprop/plannotator`, then `droid plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Commands only, no plan interception yet. | [README](apps/droid-plugin/README.md) | | **Gemini CLI** | Nothing. The hook, policy, and slash commands are configured automatically. Requires Gemini CLI 0.36.0+. | [README](apps/gemini/README.md) | | **Kiro CLI** | Nothing. Skills and an example agent are installed automatically. Try `kiro-cli chat --agent plannotator`. | [README](apps/kiro-cli/README.md) | | **OpenCode** | Add `"plugin": ["@plannotator/opencode@latest"]` to `opencode.json`. Restart OpenCode. | [README](apps/opencode-plugin/README.md) | | **Pi** | Skip the installer. Just `pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension`. Start Pi with `--plan`, or toggle with `/plannotator-plan-mode`. | [README](apps/pi-extension/README.md) | | **T3 Code** | For Claude threads in T3: run `plannotator t3 --help` and follow its two steps (sign in to T3 once, add the `--t3` MCP entry). Your Inbox replies then arrive in the thread as new turns. Codex threads in T3 get them too when T3 runs on the same computer, with nothing more to set up. | [README](packages/t3-code/README.md) | **Updating:** run the installer again for the binary and slash commands. It also updates an installed Claude Code plugin when the `claude` command is on your PATH (opt out with `--skip-claude-plugin`); otherwise run `claude plugin marketplace update plannotator`, then `claude plugin update plannotator@plannotator`, then restart Claude Code (refreshing the marketplace alone does not update the plugin). Pi: `pi update --extensions` (a plain `pi update` updates only Pi). On Claude Code 2.1.287 or newer, plan review, code review and annotate don't make Claude wait: Claude ends its turn and your decision arrives later as a message. Set `PLANNOTATOR_CLAUDE_MOD=0` to go back to the classic flow. Full walkthroughs live in the [installation docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation). ### Uninstall The safe default removes recognized Plannotator-installed components and keeps your local plans, history, drafts, guides, and settings: ```bash plannotator uninstall ``` Use `--purge` for a full removal of known local Plannotator data as well: ```bash plannotator uninstall --purge ```
What uninstall removes, what it keeps, and when it stops Purge requires typing `purge` at the prompt and explains that the data is local-only: it is not stored on a Plannotator server and cannot be recovered. For automation, pass `--yes` (or `-y`); non-interactive removal refuses to run without it. Use `--dry-run` to preview recognized work without making changes. Host integrations are always part of uninstall. If a broken or unavailable host prevents safe cleanup, the command names the blocking plugin manager or configuration, gives exact manual cleanup instructions, and stops before deleting the binary. Complete that cleanup and rerun uninstall. It also keeps the binary when an agent's config file can't be read (another tool's too), or when a hook it did not install still runs Plannotator. The error names the file, the tool, and what to do. A `plannotator-inbox` entry you added yourself, or a Claude Code or Droid plugin installed for one project, is named with how to remove it and does not keep the binary. These mechanics keep the ordinary confirmation default-negative, make the irreversible outcome require a stronger explicit word, and still give package managers and scripts a conventional non-interactive flag. The command covers the conventional macOS, Linux, WSL, and Windows binary locations; the managed `sem` sidecar and agent-terminal runtime; installer skills, commands, hooks, policies, caches, and recognizable Amp/Kiro files; and detected Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Droid, Pi, and VS Code installations through their host CLIs. Shared JSONC settings are edited surgically, while strict JSON updates preserve the file's indentation, line endings, and trailing-newline style. Custom or unrecognized files, separately installed optional skills, project-local integrations, external plan-save locations, and invalid configs are preserved (malformed host config is a fail-safe error). If cleanup reports an error, the CLI remains available for a safe retry, and its Windows PATH entry is retained or restored when possible. If PATH restoration itself fails, the output gives the full CLI path for retry and asks for manual PATH repair. For safety, purge refuses filesystem roots, the home directory, the shared temporary directory, symlinked data directories, and non-directory data paths. Existing paths are compared by filesystem identity, so case aliases, symlinks, hardlinks, and bind mounts cannot bypass the root/home/ancestor checks. That identity and every containment guard are revalidated after awaited host commands, immediately before the synchronous data-removal block; a replaced data directory is refused without touching either the old or replacement data. If your dedicated data directory is symlinked, point `PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` at its resolved target and retry.
If you installed only the standalone Pi extension and do not have the `plannotator` CLI, use `pi remove npm:@plannotator/pi-extension`.
Claude Code: manual hook setup (without the plugin system) Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "hooks": { "PermissionRequest": [ { "matcher": "ExitPlanMode", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "plannotator", "timeout": 345600 } ] } ] } } ```
Pin a specific version ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --version vX.Y.Z ``` ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1))) -Version vX.Y.Z ```
### Try it The fastest way to see what Plannotator does is to invoke it yourself, right now, from your agent: ``` /plannotator-last # annotate the agent's last reply /plannotator-review # review your current diff, PR-style /plannotator-annotate report.html # annotate any file, folder, or URL ``` (Slash commands in most agents; `$plannotator-*` skills in Codex, command palette in Amp.) Plan review needs no command at all. The next time your agent proposes a plan, it opens in your browser automatically. --- ## How it works ### Plan review ``` Agent calls ExitPlanMode -> PermissionRequest hook fires -> Local server reads plan from hook input -> Browser opens with review UI -> You annotate and approve/deny -> Approve: agent proceeds -> Deny: structured feedback sent to agent -> Agent revises, plan diff shows what changed ``` ### Code review ``` You run /plannotator-review -> git diff captures changes (or PR fetched by URL) -> Browser opens with diff viewer -> Annotate lines, stage/unstage files -> Send feedback: returned to agent session -> Approve: "LGTM" sent ``` --- ## Integrations **VS Code**: Open plans in editor tabs, view diffs inline, add annotations from the editor gutter. Install from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=backnotprop.plannotator-webview). **Obsidian**: Auto-save approved plans to a vault with YAML frontmatter, tags from the plan title, and backlinks for graph connectivity. Configure in Plannotator's Settings panel. **Bear**: Save plans as Bear notes with nested tags and project metadata. **Notion**: Save plans as Markdown child pages under a shared Notion page. Set `NOTION_TOKEN` in the environment that starts Plannotator, then configure the parent page in Settings. **GitHub / GitLab**: Pass any PR or MR URL to `/plannotator-review` and review it with the full diff viewer, annotations, and file tree. --- ## Remote / SSH / devcontainer Plannotator auto-detects SSH sessions and switches to fixed port `19432`. For a different port, or in a devcontainer or Docker: ```bash export PLANNOTATOR_REMOTE=1 export PLANNOTATOR_PORT=9999 # forward this port ``` VS Code devcontainers forward the port automatically (check the Ports tab). For raw SSH, add this to `~/.ssh/config`, using your `PLANNOTATOR_PORT` value if you set one: ``` Host your-server LocalForward 19432 localhost:19432 ``` In remote mode the server listens on every interface (`0.0.0.0`) with no login, so anyone who can reach the port can use it, even when you use an SSH tunnel. Keep the port closed to networks you don't trust. --- ## Security Every released binary ships with a SHA256 sidecar. [SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/) attestations are available from v0.17.2. The current release workflow also attaches a CycloneDX JSON SBOM, evaluates it with a fresh Grype database before anything is attested or published, and creates a GitHub/Sigstore SBOM attestation for the shipped binaries and npm tarballs. The SBOM is intentionally labeled as a release-wide Syft inventory of the monorepo's locked build inputs and dependencies. It is not an exact per-binary runtime inventory: Bun standalone executables do not expose their bundled JavaScript package metadata to Syft. The canonical [installation and verification docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation#pin-or-verify-a-release) cover the existing installer path; the exact new SBOM commands are included below and must be copied to that Mintlify page before the first SBOM-enabled release. The release gate rejects scanner-side ignored matches and treats unknown applicability conservatively as runtime when evaluating CISA KEV and fixable Critical findings. Its explicit Grype configuration, complete JSON results, database status, and repository policy decision remain available as workflow evidence. To verify a released Linux x64 binary, its existing provenance, and the new SBOM evidence directly: ```bash tag=vX.Y.Z version="${tag#v}" mkdir -p /tmp/plannotator-release-verify gh release download "$tag" --repo backnotprop/plannotator \ --pattern 'plannotator-linux-x64*' \ --pattern "plannotator-${version}-release-sbom.cdx.json*" \ --dir /tmp/plannotator-release-verify (cd /tmp/plannotator-release-verify && sha256sum --check plannotator-linux-x64.sha256) (cd /tmp/plannotator-release-verify && sha256sum --check "plannotator-${version}-release-sbom.cdx.json.sha256") gh attestation verify /tmp/plannotator-release-verify/plannotator-linux-x64 \ --repo backnotprop/plannotator --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" \ --signer-workflow backnotprop/plannotator/.github/workflows/release.yml \ --predicate-type https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 gh attestation verify /tmp/plannotator-release-verify/plannotator-linux-x64 \ --repo backnotprop/plannotator --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" \ --signer-workflow backnotprop/plannotator/.github/workflows/release.yml \ --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom ``` These are separate claims over the same artifact digest: provenance identifies its builder/source/workflow, while the CycloneDX predicate describes the release-wide inventory. The release runbook also canonicalizes the downloaded SBOM and attested predicate with `jq -S` and compares them. To verify on install: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --verify-attestation ``` Requires the `gh` CLI, but no login: the installer fetches the attestation bundle from GitHub's public attestations API and verifies it with `gh attestation verify --bundle` (the extraction needs node, python3, or jq on PATH; gh's authenticated fetch is the fallback). Can also be set persistently in `~/.plannotator/config.json`: ```json { "verifyAttestation": true } ``` Installer verification remains opt-in and verifies SLSA build provenance; normal installation does not requir

# 技能管理 / Skill manager

左侧栏的全局入口，打开一个跨会话的技能管理页，用来集中查看和切换当前会被本地技能提供器扫描到的技能。它不只展示目录，还可以直接改写每个技能的调用开关。

> 维护/开发请先读源码仓库里的 `AGENTS.md`：架构、数据流、踩过的坑、重载与测试命令都在那里。本文只面向使用者。

- **按来源分组**：页面从上到下依次是用户 `~/.dsh/skills`、用户 `~/.agents/skills`、自定义目录、内置（安装包内的扫描根），然后是项目 `.dsh/skills`、项目 `.agents/skills`。项目根按已注册的工作区逐个解析（最近的 `.git` 祖先），因此不同会话所在的仓库都能出现在同一页。
- **数据来源**：页面直接扫描这些根目录，而不是查询全局技能注册表。技能的识别规则与本地提供器一致：顶层目录里的 `SKILL.md` 或顶层的 `*.md` 文件，frontmatter 必须有合法的 kebab-case `name`、非空 `description`，两个 invocation 字段如果出现，必须是可识别的布尔写法（`true/false/yes/no/on/off/1/0`）。扫描根取自宿主当前组合里的技能提供器配置，包括预设 `dsh-agent-preset` 子行声明的自定义目录。
- **两个可见性开关**：取消「对模型可见」会写入 `disable-model-invocation: true`，取消「用户可调用」会写入 `user-invocable: false`；重新勾选会移除对应字段，恢复默认允许。只改动 `SKILL.md` frontmatter 中的这两个顶级键，其余 frontmatter、注释和正文保持不变。
- **立即生效**：写入后向 `fs/observed` 发送与内建 `edit`/`write` 工具相同的变更观察，技能提供器会同步失效并重新扫描；宿主没有 `fs` 服务、走本地文件回退写时同样发送。写入完成后直接读回该文件确认两个字段已是目标状态。
- **扫描根只读展示**：直接展示当前生效的技能根路径与存在状态，不提供新增、删除或修改配置的操作；不存在的目录默认隐藏，标题右侧的按钮可以按需显示；全局目录排在项目根之前。存在的根可以点「打开文件夹」在系统文件管理器中打开。
- **打开文件夹**：Windows 上通过编码后的文件 URI 交给 Explorer，并保留可见窗口——隐藏式启动会连 Explorer 的文件夹窗口一起藏掉，这个坑已经规避；安装包（`.asar`）里的目录无法用文件管理器打开，按钮会禁用并说明原因。
- **安全边界**：服务端每次请求都重新计算当前扫描结果，只接受确实出现在扫描结果里的文件路径；改写前会检查 frontmatter 结构。写入带版本保护：读内容和写盘之间文件被其他程序改动，会返回冲突（`stale_file`）而不是覆盖。宿主提供 `fs` 服务时用它的版本令牌，回退到本地文件写入时用文件的修改时间与大小，两条路都有保护；回退写的临时文件在失败时会删除。

## 限制

- 只显示本地文件系统里的技能：页面只认识本地技能提供器的扫描根。插件用 `ctx.skills.register()` / `registerProvider()` 注册的运行时技能不会出现，也不计入统计——包括随安装包分发的 office、visualize、official-plugins、personalized-pages 等内置技能，它们没有扫描根。
- 同名的技能如果被更高优先级扫描根覆盖，会带 `shadowed` 标记，页面提示里说明改动不影响模型看到的版本；文件层没有可写的 dedupe 信息，所以不会隐藏这些行。
- 内置安装归档（`app.asar`）里的扫描根按「内置」分组展示：行上标「位于安装包内，只读」，两个开关禁用；即使绕过页面直接调用接口，服务端也会以 `read_only_source` 拒绝改写。本机这个根是预设声明的 `dsh-agent-preset/skills`（当前只有 `dsh-doc`），它本身在提供器里算自定义目录，页面按安装包位置把它显示为内置。
- 只编辑 `disable-model-invocation` 与 `user-invocable` 两个字段，不支持编辑技能正文、名称或描述。
- 页面通过宿主 `/api` 路由读取数据，因此需要 Harness 的 Web 端连接；宿主半未加载时页面会显示错误并可重试。

## 安装

这是一个本地 Bundle：`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向 `cordis.patch.yml`，后者只插入一个宿主插件行；浏览器半通过 `dsh.client` 声明为 Web 平台入口。装好后左侧栏出现「技能管理」入口。

1. **解压到长期保留的目录**。本地 Bundle 是链接安装：DSH 只记下这个目录的路径，不复制文件。之后移动或删除目录，插件会失效。
2. 打开 DSH Desktop 的 **插件（Plugins）** → **添加插件（Add plugin）**，选择 `package.json` 所在的那个目录。
3. 左侧栏出现「技能管理」即安装完成。页面若提示宿主半未加载，重启一次 Desktop 再打开。
4. 卸载在插件列表里移除该 Bundle，不会删除你的目录。

包内自带测试，解压后可以自检（需要本机有 Node.js 18 及以上）：

```powershell
npm test
```

要求 **DSH Desktop 0.2.2-rc.5 或更新版本**（`package.json` 的 `engines.dsh` 会校验）：插件通过 `connection.fetch` 注册 `/api` 路由，并读取 `configEditor` 的当前组合，旧版本没有这些接口。页面依赖 Harness 的 Web 端连接，纯 headless 环境看不到这个入口。

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT grant, engines.dsh at least 0.2.2-rc.5 and documented local installation match the two native modules. Connection.fetch registration requires the service; absent service leaves the plugin inactive. SKILL.md frontmatter writes use expected-version checks and atomic replacement; OS reveal commands and local skill discovery remain sensitive capabilities. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-run-code-itself

Data-Code Separation for DSH PTC.

The direct tool stays run_code. Every call preloads two variables:

- run_code_itself: the complete arguments of this call, including all sibling fields;
- run_code_subtools: every tool exposes DSH's original description, parameters, and output schema; the system prompt lists common tools as compact signatures and other tools by name only.

Only run_code is callable directly. Every other tool is called from inside the program. The goal is simple: keep data out of the code string, and pass subtool arguments as real JSON objects rather than JSON strings.

For PTC runtimes configured as script or repl, the plugin wraps the program in an async IIFE. The two prelude variables remain local, top-level return/await keep function-body semantics, and a second evaluation cannot hit a duplicate const declaration.

## What it does

Instead of this:

    const svg = "<svg>...</svg>"
    await tools.write({ file_path: "out.svg", content: svg })

write this:

    {"code":"return await tools.write(run_code_itself.write)","description":"Write SVG","write":{"file_path":"out.svg","content":"<svg>...</svg>"}}

or build a schema-informed direct call:

    {"code":"const s = run_code_subtools.write.parameters; if (!s.required.every(k => k in run_code_itself.write)) throw new Error('missing write fields'); return (await tools.write(run_code_itself.write)).path","description":"Write file","write":{"file_path":"a.txt","content":"hi"}}

Array and loop:

    {"code":"const out = []; for (const e of run_code_itself.edits) out.push(await tools.edit(e)); return out.map(r => r.path)","description":"Apply edits","edits":[{"file_path":"a.ts","old_string":"old","new_string":"new"},{"file_path":"b.ts","old_string":"old2","new_string":"new2"}]}

run_code_subtools is a plain JSON object keyed by tool name; every entry carries the complete description + parameters + output schema for on-demand loading. The system prompt only lists common signatures and other tool names.

There are no generated templates. run_code_subtools.<tool>.parameters is the tool's original input JSON Schema for every tool; build the argument object directly in a sibling field and let the tool schema validate it. run_code_subtools.<tool>.output is the original output schema. The prompt's signature is only a compact hint for non-common tools.

## System guide and tool description

The system prompt contains:

- Data-Code Separation rules, rewritten from the stock PTC wording;
- common tools with compact signatures, other tools by name only;
- runtime metadata exposing { description, parameters, output } for every tool, available on demand through run_code_subtools.

The run_code tool description is rewritten too; it preserves the runtime execution instructions, current-directory text, and sandbox guidance. The system guide is longer than the tool description.

The persona must use complete: false. With complete: true, the system-prompt guide is suppressed.

## Prompt techniques

These settings belong to a profile or dsh_home patch, not to the plugin's own cordis.patch.yml. The plugin-level file stays an empty array ([]); it only makes the plugin available and is mounted by the profile or preset.

### Remove the harness identity globally

    - id: harness-dev-context
      disabled: true
    - id: system-prompt
      config:
        includeHarnessIdentity: false

This removes the implementation-checkout / Web-GUI context and the harness identity text from the global system prompt.

### Persona

Use this as the persona prefix; complete must remain false so the system guide is not suppressed:

    - id: persona
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
      config:
        prefix: |
          You are a helpful software engineer assistant. You MUST follow the run_code usage rules in the run_code tool description. Never inline subtool arguments. Put them as real JSON objects in run_code_itself sibling fields; inspect run_code_subtools.<tool>.parameters when needed, and return only JSON-safe values.
        complete: false
        includeRuntimeContext: false

If you run several presets, add the same persona entry to each preset's plugin list.

### AGENTS.md emphasis

Append a short section to the user/workspace AGENTS.md:

    ## run_code Data-Code Separation

    - Never inline tools.x({...}) inside run_code code.
    - Put data and every subtool argument in sibling fields of the call.
    - Read run_code_itself sibling fields; inspect run_code_subtools.<tool>.parameters when needed; return only JSON-safe values.
    - If a value needs quotes, backslashes, or newlines, move it to a sibling field.

The repository's own cordis.patch.yml is deliberately []; do not copy the profile rows above into it.

## Mount

Preset:

    - id: run-code-itself
      name: 'dsh-run-code-itself'

Host row:

    - insert:
        - id: run-code-itself
          name: 'dsh-run-code-itself'

## Install

    dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh-run-code-itself

## Configuration

- maxSubCallsPerMinute: nested tool-call attempts per minute of run_code timeout.
- maxParallelSubCalls: maximum overlapping concurrency-safe program subcalls.
- commonTools: tools listed with compact signatures in the system prompt; all other tools are names only there. run_code_subtools always has full description + parameters + output for every tool. Default: bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, read_image.
- promptMode and sdkStyle: deprecated, accepted for compatibility, ignored.

Example profile config:

    config:
      commonTools:
        - bash
        - read
        - write
        - edit
        - glob
        - grep
        - read_image

## Why the tool name is still run_code

A previous experimental version exposed the tool as program. Three independent reviews found that a plugin-level alias breaks DSH invariants: tool/call logs, session migration, approval and presentCall paths, and knownNames/tool ordering all bind the real name. The final version keeps run_code and puts the Data-Code Separation investment into variables, schemas, the system guide, and the tool description instead.

## Behaviour and limits

- Targets the TypeScript PTC runtime. The plugin does not import or switch to a Python PTC runtime.
- The plugin does not hard-enforce Code-Data Separation. General TypeScript can still construct argument objects in code; prompt compliance is model-dependent.
- A small cross-model check showed OpenAI and Google models following the guide; a DeepSeek-flash route reverted to inline calls on complex tasks.
- If deterministic enforcement is required, use runtime provenance or a no-code pipeline; neither is implemented here.

## Development

    DSH_PACKAGES_DIR=... node --experimental-loader ./test/loader.mjs ./test/run.mjs

The test covers schema, guide length, tool schemas, injection, special payloads, alias dispatch, and preset mounting.

Fixed prompt data lives under prompts/: guide.md and tool-description.txt. index.js only loads and renders it.

MIT.

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT grant, versioned DSH peers/engines, native PtcExecutor subclass and all three fixed prompt files are present. The deliberately empty bundle patch is documented: local-directory installation exposes the module and a separately documented Host or preset row mounts it. It rewrites run_code metadata, system prompts and per-agent execution plumbing; prompt compliance is not deterministic enforcement. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-astryx

Watches `@astryxdesign` (Astryx) releases and says whether the newest Astryx still fits this plugin's support contract — and self-checks whether the Astryx MCP server and skill in this DSH install actually work.

Astryx is a beta design system (`@astryxdesign/core`, 0.7.x) whose CLI is deliberately the agent interface: `astryx docs`, `astryx component <Name>`, `astryx manifest --json`, `astryx mcp`. Beta means that surface moves. An agent that learns Astryx once and never re-checks will confidently write code against commands that no longer exist. This plugin is the guard: it watches the registry and it checks the local wiring.

## Tools

### `astryx_status`

Versions, update availability, and a compatibility verdict. Cached for `ttlHours`; pass `refresh: true` to re-check now.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `astryx.installedCore` / `installedCli` / `installedSource` | what the project has: `node_modules` (accurate), `package.json` ranges, or `none` |
| `astryx.latestCore` / `latestCli` / `canaryCore` | npm `dist-tags` |
| `astryx.updateAvailable` | an install exists and differs from latest (never true on an empty project) |
| `compat.verdict` | always judged against the **newest** release — see below |
| `probe` | `astryx manifest --json` from the project CLI, then any global install: version and any missing required command |

| Verdict | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `compatible` | newest release is inside `supported` and equals `testedAgainst` | nothing |
| `compatible-untested` | inside the range but newer than anything verified | run `astryx_selfcheck`, then bump `testedAgainst` |
| `plugin-update-required` | newest release is **outside** this plugin's range | update this plugin, or pin `@astryxdesign/core` |
| `astryx-too-old` | below the supported minimum | upgrade Astryx |
| `capability-incompatible` | the CLI answered but a required command or flag is gone, whatever the version says | update `compat.json` and the plugin |
| `unknown` | registry unreachable and nothing installed | retry with `refresh: true` |

Version numbers and surface facts are judged separately on purpose: a release can keep its version shape and still drop a command.

### `astryx_selfcheck`

Read-only. Reports facts and one failure code; repairs nothing.

1. **Plugin** — the `dsh-astryx` row in the applied patch layers (bundle patches → profile patch → home patch, later wins) and whether it is disabled. The tool being callable is itself the registration proof.
2. **CLI** — resolvable, and does `astryx manifest --json` still expose every command in `compat.json`?
3. **MCP** — is an Astryx `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row configured? If it is stdio, one `initialize` → `tools/list` handshake reports tool count and latency. With no row, the local `astryx mcp` is probed and labelled `basis: "local-cli"` (on 0.7.17 it answers with its full tool list, 56 tools).
4. **Skill** — Astryx writes its skill to `~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md`. DSH loads skills from both `$DSH_HOME/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, so the verdicts are `effective` (in a loaded root, valid frontmatter), `project-only` (an `astryx-project` skill inside this repo only), `invalid` (frontmatter missing `name`/`description`) and `missing`. `roots` lists the directories that were checked.
5. **Project** — whether this directory uses Astryx and whether `astryx init` already wrote its managed `ASTRYX:` block into `AGENTS.md`.

Failure codes: `plugin-row-missing`, `plugin-row-disabled`, `mcp-unreachable`, `skill-invalid`, `contract-drift`.

## Install

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  →  /Users/chrischen/projects/dsh-astryx
```

One row, `dsh-astryx`, with the defaults below.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ttlHours` | `6` | how long a status result stays fresh |
| `checkOnStart` | `true` | warm the cache once after activation (non-blocking, unref'd timer) |
| `registry` | `https://registry.npmjs.org` | dist-tags endpoint base |
| `projectPath` | `''` → `process.cwd()` | default directory to search for an Astryx project |

## Cross-platform

The Host runs inside Electron: `process.execPath` is the app binary, and a Finder/Explorer launch inherits a short `PATH`. Nothing here relies on either.

- **Global CLI lookup** (`src/npmPrefixes.js`) — npm puts packages under `<prefix>/lib/node_modules` (POSIX) or `<prefix>/node_modules` (Windows). Prefixes come from `npm_config_prefix`, `PNPM_HOME`, `~/.npmrc`, `%APPDATA%\npm`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm`, `/usr/local`, `/opt/homebrew/lib/nodejs`, `~/.nvm`, `~/.asdf`, `~/.volta`, `~/Library/pnpm`, plus versioned Node installs one level down. `PATH` and `execPath` are extra hints, never the only source.
- **Spawning** (`src/spawn.js`) — global CLIs run as `node <entry.mjs>`, identically on every OS. A `.cmd`/`.bat` shim is the last resort and is spawned through a shell with pre-quoted arguments, because Node ≥ 20 refuses to spawn one directly.
- **Files** — every path goes through `node:path`; patch and skill text is CRLF-normalised before parsing; `.gitattributes` pins LF for hashed content.
- **CI** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the suite and `npm pack --dry-run` on `ubuntu`, `macos` and `windows` × Node 22/24.

## Compatibility policy

`compat.json` is the contract: `supported` (the range the guidance is written for), `testedAgainst` (the release actually verified), `requiredCommands` / `requiredInitFlags` (the CLI surface the guidance depends on). Bump `testedAgainst` after a probe pass, widen `supported` only after reading the release notes, and change `required*` when the guidance itself changes. Nothing here pins `@astryxdesign/*`: the plugin reads versions, it never installs them.

## Degraded modes

- **No Astryx installed** — `astryx_status` still answers, judging the newest release from the registry against the contract.
- **No network** — the verdict falls back to the installed version; `registry.ok` is `false` with the error.
- **No CLI** — version facts still work; `probe.ran` is `false` and `capability-incompatible` cannot trigger.
- **Streamable-HTTP MCP rows** — reported as configured but not probed; this plugin speaks JSON-RPC over stdio only.

## Layout

```
index.js            Host plugin: two tools, one prompt section, warm check
compat.json         support contract (versions + required CLI surface)
src/semver.js       minimal semver (comparators, prerelease ordering)
src/contract.js     contract loader
src/registry.js     npm dist-tags (failures stay data)
src/npmPrefixes.js  npm global prefix discovery, PATH-independent
src/spawn.js        cross-platform spawn planning (.cmd quoting)
src/project.js      project lookup, installed versions, CLI manifest probe
src/compat.js       verdict logic
src/cache.js        ttl cache under $DSH_HOME/cache/dsh-astryx
src/status.js       status assembly + text renderer
src/paths.js        DSH locations and skill roots from the environment
src/patchScan.js    applied patch layers (bundles → profile → home), line-based
src/skills.js       skill presence, visibility, frontmatter validity
src/mcpProbe.js     one-shot MCP initialize → tools/list
src/selfcheck.js    the self-check report
```

Tests: `node --test test/` (75 cases, no network).

## Publishing to the plugin market

Ready: `dsh.bundle.patch`, namespaced row id, icon, en/zh locale, README as the detail page, CI matrix.

The catalog entry is prepared at [`market/chrischjh__dsh-astryx.yml`](market/chrischjh__dsh-astryx.yml) — it is copied verbatim into `awesome-dsh-plugin` as `data/plugins/chrischjh__dsh-astryx.yml` (category `dev`, raster icon from `assets/`).

Done: public repo, `repository`/`homepage`/`bugs`, `dsh-plugin` topic, green CI on three platforms, packed-tarball install verified.

Done: `npm publish` (2FA web-auth through the browser) — `dsh-astryx@0.2.0` is live and the registry picked up `repository`, so npm download counts attach to the listing automatically.

Still pending: the catalog PR, once the repo is a day old (the project is new; a same-day submission reads as spam). The entry is ready to copy verbatim into `awesome-dsh-plugin` as `data/plugins/chrischjh__dsh-astryx.yml`.

## Known limits

- Patch scanning is line-based YAML tuned to the row shapes DSH writes; unusual nesting is reported as not found rather than guessed.
- A skill written into a loaded root appears in the DSH catalog at the next session start, not mid-session.
- `astryx_status` judges the newest release; it does not predict what a future release will break.

# 蕾米埃尔桌宠 · dsh-pet-remielle-desktop

把「小蕾米 · 全帧版」的 754 帧素材做成**常驻 Windows 桌面**的桌宠：透明置顶窗、原生分辨率动画、能在桌面上直接和 DSH 智能体对话和派活。

> A transparent, always-on-top desktop pet for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh) on Windows. 754 hand-cleaned frames, real DSH agent chat, four-way smart layout.

![桌宠](docs/pet.png)
![聊天](docs/chat.png)

## 是什么

- **真桌面窗**：独立的 Neutralino 窗口（透明 / 无边框 / 置顶 / 不进任务栏），不是网页里的浮层。播放 6 个状态的原生 340×304 动画 WebP：待机、思考、工具调用、边想边写、等待、完成，全部按原始帧率 30 ms 播放，放大也不糊。
- **能干活**：桌面上发一句话，她就真的开一个 DSH 智能体会话去干活（默认当前工作区、workspace-write 权限）。她调工具、跑命令、读文件的过程就是她自己在 DSH 里的过程；会话同时出现在 DSH Web GUI 的会话列表里，可以接着聊、接着派活。
- **四向自适应**：宠物在屏幕右半边时聊天卡片向左展开，在左半边时向右展开；靠近屏幕顶部/底部时卡片自动下移/上抬。开合聊天时宠物本人的屏幕位置一动不动。
- **图片与 emoji**：输入框旁的 ＋ 可以发图片（png/jpg/webp/gif/bmp，最多 4 张）给她看；她回复里的 emoji 正常彩色渲染，回复中的图片路径/URL 也会内联成缩略图，点一下看大图。
- **全屏让位**：前台是全屏游戏或全屏视频时，自动取消置顶并隐藏，退出全屏自动回来（不会盖在游戏上）。
- **可收起、可退出**：宠物右上角悬浮 − / + / ×，调整大小（0.5×–2×，0.25 步进）和收起成 64×64 圆形徽章；右键菜单可以真正退出（窗口与进程一起结束）。
- **记得住**：对话、窗口位置、缩放都落盘；重启 DSH 之后接着上次继续。

## 安装

要求：Windows 10/11、DSH 0.2.x 及以上。运行时（Neutralino）已随包内置，安装时不跑任何构建脚本，不需要 allowBuilds。

### 从 GitHub 安装

```
plugin_manager install_bundle target="github:Cyrus0719/dsh-pet-remielle"
```

命令行等价写法：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Cyrus0719/dsh-pet-remielle
```

### 从 npm 安装

```
plugin_manager install_bundle target="npm:dsh-pet-remielle-desktop"
```

命令行等价写法：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-pet-remielle-desktop
```

### 从本地目录安装

```
plugin_manager install_bundle target="file:C:/Users/<你>/dsh-pet-remielle"
```

安装完成即启用（cordis.patch.yml 里插入 pet-remielle），桌面上应该出现蕾米埃尔。窗口没出现时检查插件条目是不是 active；改过插件代码后需要重载：把条目关掉再打开一次。

如果 runtime/neutralino-win_x64.exe 丢了（比如你只复制了部分文件），执行 node scripts/install-neutralino.mjs 重新下载。

### 卸载

```
plugin_manager remove_bundle target="dsh-pet-remielle-desktop"
```

再删掉 %USERPROFILE%\\.dsh\\desktop-pet（对话、位置、缩放记忆都在里面）。
## 用

| 操作 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 单击宠物 | 开 / 关聊天卡片 |
| 右键宠物 | 和她聊天 / 新开一个会话 / 在 DSH 里打开这个会话 / 收起 / 退出蕾米埃尔 |
| 宠物右上角悬浮 − / + | 缩小 / 放大（0.5×–2×，0.25 步进，记住） |
| 宠物右上角悬浮 × | 收起成 64×64 圆形徽章，点徽章恢复 |
| 拖动宠物 | 换位置（记住） |
| 聊天头部 ⟲ / ↗ / × | 新会话 / 在 DSH Web GUI 打开该会话 / 收起聊天 |
| 输入框 ＋ | 选图片发给她（最多 4 张） |
| Enter / Shift+Enter | 发送 / 换行 |

「退出蕾米埃尔」会结束窗口和它自己的进程，但不改插件开关：重启 DSH 或把插件关掉再打开，她就回来了。只想暂时收起来用「收起」。

## 数据放在哪

- `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\desktop-pet\chat.json` — 最近 60 条对话 + 当前会话 id
- `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\desktop-pet\position.json` — 窗口坐标
- `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\desktop-pet\ui.json` — 缩放比例

对话本体在 DSH 会话里（chat.json 只是摘录），所以在 DSH Web GUI 的会话历史里能看到同一个 session，可以继续聊。

## 宠物素材与状态

`assets/pets/remielle/pet.json`：

```json
{
  "id": "remielle",
  "displayName": "蕾米埃尔",
  "cell": [340, 304],
  "animations": {
    "idle": "anims/idle.webp",
    "thinking": "anims/thinking.webp",
    "tool": "anims/tool.webp",
    "review": "anims/review.webp",
    "waiting": "anims/waiting.webp",
    "done": "anims/done.webp"
  }
}
```

想换成别的宠物：在 `assets/pets/<id>/` 放同名结构的 `pet.json` + 透明动画 WebP，然后把 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的 `petId` 改掉；也可以放进 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\desktop-pet\pets\<id>\`（用户目录优先于包内）。

## 实现说明

- 窗口后端、状态机、宠物目录约定来自 [dsh-desktop-pet](https://github.com/sereinmono/dsh-desktop-pet)（MIT）。
- 本包在它基础上做的事：原生分辨率动画帧流（不再用 8×9 精灵图）、聊天卡片（真实 DSH 会话 / 图片 / emoji / 四向布局 / 自动滚到底）、状态机修复（`tool/result` 不回落导致"一直画画"、断开会话残留任务）、全屏让位、缩放与位置持久化、收起徽章、去托盘。
- 前端是 `assets/neutralino/resources/index.html` 一份文件；host 是 `lib/index.js`。

## 素材与署名（重要）

- 素材作者：**HanaAyane / 小蕾米** — https://github.com/HanaAyane/remielle-codex-pet
- 衍生自《绝区零》同人素材，动作经人工逐帧整理 + AI 辅助重绘；本包只做格式转换（GIF → 透明 WebP）。
- **仅限个人非商业同人使用**：禁止销售、付费分发、改名冒充、商标注册，禁止暗示米哈游 / HoYoverse 官方授权。转发请保留署名与仓库链接。
- 详见 [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) 与 [ASSET-USAGE.md](ASSET-USAGE.md)。

## 许可

代码：MIT（见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)，含上游 dsh-desktop-pet 的 MIT 声明）。
内置宠物素材：不适用 MIT，版权归 HanaAyane / 小蕾米，仅限个人非商业同人使用。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-civ6

让 AI 在 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（DSH）的会话里玩《文明6》。思考和行动的是 DSH 自己的模型，用的是 DSH 的额度，**不需要另配 API Key**。

```
DSH 会话 ──(MCP, stdio)──> civ6-mcp（Python）──(Tuner 调试端口 4318)──> 文明6
```

插件本身不碰游戏。它在所有会话里加一个 `civ6` 工具，由它在后台拉起 [civ6-mcp](https://github.com/Darianliu23/civ6-mcp)；civ6-mcp 通过游戏的调试端口读取局面、发出操作，所有操作都走游戏自己的规则。

## 三种玩法

在 DSH 的插件设置里选“玩法”，**改了马上生效**：AI 下一次动作时会自动切换，并先重新读一遍新玩法的规则。不用重启 DSH，也不用新建会话。

| 玩法 | AI 能做什么 | 适合 |
|---|---|---|
| 一起玩（默认） | 全部操作（61 个动作），但按你的话来；不经你同意不结束回合 | 边聊边玩，分工合作 |
| AI 当助理 | **只能查询**（31 个动作），不能动游戏。你问它答，给具体建议 | 自己玩，要个参谋 |
| AI 自己玩 | 全部操作。自己一回合一回合地打，每隔几回合汇报一次 | 想看 AI 打 |

动作数是原版规则下的数字（隐藏了原版没有的总督、着力点、世界议会）。

**随时接手**（“一起玩”和“AI 自己玩”）：说“我来”“停一下”，AI 会交出操作权，之后它所有改动游戏的操作都会被 civ6-mcp 拒绝，只能查询和给建议；说“你来”“继续”再交还给它。想立刻打断正在进行的操作，点 DSH 的停止按钮。

## 任何会话都能玩

不用选预设，**已经聊过的会话也能玩**：插件在所有会话里加了一个 `civ6` 工具。

- 常驻上下文里只有这一个工具的简短说明，不会把六十多个游戏工具塞进每个会话；
- 想玩时直接说“来玩文明6”，AI 会先调 `{"action":"help"}` 读规则和动作列表，之后每个动作都是 `{"action":"动作名","args":{参数}}`；
- 第一次用到时插件才在后台启动 civ6-mcp；
- 游戏没开或没进对局时，会直接告诉 AI 连不上，不会卡住。

以前的三个会话预设还在，默认不创建。用预设建过会话的，在设置里把对应的预设打开，老会话就能接着用。

## 需要什么

1. **文明6**（Steam 版）。打开 Tuner：选项里的 “Tuner (disables achievements)”，或者在游戏关着时把
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Firaxis Games\Sid Meier's Civilization VI\AppOptions.txt` 里的 `EnableTuner 0` 改成 `EnableTuner 1`。
   开着 Tuner 时**成就会被禁用**。另外关掉“自动结束回合”，用窗口化。不需要装 SDK。
2. **civ6-mcp**（`base-game-compat` 分支）和 [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)：

   ```bash
   git clone -b base-game-compat https://github.com/Darianliu23/civ6-mcp.git
   ```

   ```bash
   cd civ6-mcp
   ```

   ```bash
   uv sync
   ```

   uv 会自动下载需要的 Python（3.12）。克隆到用户目录下的 `civ6-mcp` 或 `Projects\civ6-mcp` 时插件能自己找到，放在别处就在插件配置里填路径。
3. **DSH**。

## 安装插件

在 DSH 的插件市场搜 `dsh-civ6` 安装，或者在插件页面用 `github:Darianliu23/dsh-civ6` 安装。装好后重启一次 DSH。

DSH 的桌面版和网页版用不同的 profile，要用哪个就在哪个里装。

<details>
<summary>从本地文件夹装（开发时）</summary>

在 `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/desktop`（或 `web`）里：

1. `package.json` 的 `dependencies` 加 `"dsh-civ6": "link:<本仓库路径>"`，`dsh.profile.bundles` 加 `"dsh-civ6"`；
2. 用 DSH 自带的 pnpm 运行 `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile`；
3. 重启 DSH。

</details>

## 怎么玩

1. 启动文明6，进入一局对局（停在主菜单时读不到局面）。
2. 在插件设置里选好玩法，然后在任意会话里说“来玩文明6”。
3. 直接说话，比如：
   - AI 自己玩：“开始吧，目标科技胜利”
   - AI 当助理：“现在该造什么？”“这个开拓者去哪建城好？”
   - 一起玩：“开拓者原地坐城，然后你帮我选个开局生产”“这回合你来收尾”

AI 每回合结束时写的反思存在 civ6-mcp 的日记里（`~/.civ6-mcp`），按这一局合起来读，新会话可以用 `get_diary` 接着之前的思路玩。

## 设置

DSH 左侧边栏「插件」→ dsh-civ6 →「配置 ›」。前六项**改了马上生效**，不用重启。

| 设置 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 玩法 | 一起玩 | 也可以选 AI 当助理、AI 自己玩 |
| 额外要求 | 空 | 比如“走科技胜利，前 50 回合至少铺 4 座城” |
| 原版规则（没有资料片） | 开 | 隐藏原版没有的工具，并告诉 AI 忽略相关机制。启用了“风云变幻”就关掉 |
| 单个动作最长等多少分钟 | 15 | 后期结束回合要等所有电脑文明走完 |
| civ6-mcp 文件夹 | 空（自动找） | 依次找环境变量 `CIV6_MCP_DIR`、用户目录下的 `civ6-mcp` 和 `Projects\civ6-mcp`、各个盘的 `Projects\civ6-mcp` |
| uv 路径 | 空（自动找） | 找不到时填 `uv.exe` 的完整路径 |
| 在所有会话里提供 civ6 工具 | 开 | 要重启 DSH |
| 三个会话预设、名字、基础预设 | 关 | 可选。要重启 DSH 并新建会话；预设会话的玩法以预设为准，不跟着设置变 |

## 已知限制

- 只在 **Windows 11 + 原版文明6（没有资料片）** 上实际玩过（AI 自己玩到第 74 回合）。装了“风云变幻”应该也能用（上游就是按风云变幻写的），但带着这边的改动没有测过。
- **游戏顾问**（选项 → 游戏 → 教程/顾问）弹出来时，游戏会停下等人点掉，电脑文明的回合也跟着停。civ6-mcp 结束回合时会自动把它关掉；嫌烦可以直接在选项里把顾问关了。
- **游戏只接受一个 Tuner 连接**。每个会话用完 20 秒后会放开连接，所以几个会话可以轮流玩，但不能同时操作；开着 SDK 的 FireTuner.exe 也会占掉连接。
- AI 思考时游戏不会暂停。文明6 是回合制，单人游戏里这不要紧。
- 接手靠说一句话或者点停止按钮，游戏里没有快捷键。
- civ6-mcp 要自己装，插件不会自动下载。

## 致谢

civ6-mcp 来自 [lmwilki/civ6-mcp](https://github.com/lmwilki/civ6-mcp)（MIT），连接游戏的 FireTuner 协议、全部游戏工具和结束回合的逻辑都是原作者写的。[Darianliu23/civ6-mcp](https://github.com/Darianliu23/civ6-mcp) 的 `base-game-compat` 分支在它的基础上加了原版规则兼容、三种玩法、接管开关和几处修复，说明见那边的 README。

## 开发

- 改了 `lib/index.js` 的 `Config` 以后运行 `npm run build:client` 重新生成配置卡片 `lib/client.js`。
- `npm test`：`tests/gateway.test.mjs` 会真的拉起本机的 civ6-mcp 走一遍入口工具（不需要游戏开着）。

## 许可

MIT，见 `LICENSE`。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-cloud-sandbox English | [简体中文](./README.zh.md) **Linux & Windows WSL2 Docker execution-sandbox runtime plugin for DeepSeek Harness (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`).** `dsh-cloud-sandbox` isolates agent commands, interactive terminals, and user-loaded Skill scripts inside hardened Linux Docker containers — managed purely by **working directory** (zero user-account coupling), with **host-wide concurrency limits and per-workspace fair queuing** built for cloud multi-tenant deployments (supporting native Linux `/var/run/docker.sock`, Windows Docker Desktop WSL2 named pipe `\\.\pipe\docker_engine`, and direct Windows -> WSL2 Docker Engine bridging via `wsl.exe`). ## Why This Plugin Exists DeepSeek Harness's default local sandbox (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local`) enforces same-world host confinement (`bwrap` / `Landlock`). In shared Linux cloud deployments where users upload custom Skills with scripts: - Host-level `bwrap` shares the host network and breaks inside nested containers; - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-sandbox` only restricts file writes (reads pass through); - There is no per-workspace CPU/RAM/PID quota, container pool, or multi-tenant fair concurrency queue. `dsh-cloud-sandbox` implements DSH's standard capability seams (`ctx.subprocess`, optional `ctx.shell`, optional `ctx.fs`) directly over the Linux Docker Engine Unix socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`) with **zero external runtime dependencies**. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Host["DSH Linux Host Process"] direction TB C1["Cordis Context A
(ctx.subprocess / ctx.shell / ctx.fs)"] C2["Cordis Context B
(ctx.subprocess / ctx.shell / ctx.fs)"] Pool["Shared DockerRuntimePool
(Keyed purely by canonical workspaceRoot)"] WS["WorkspacePolicy
allowedBaseDirs · symlink guard · :ro Skill mounts"] Sched["Two-Tier FairScheduler
Container LRU Pool + Per-Workspace Round-Robin Queue"] Sock["Linux Docker Socket Client
/var/run/docker.sock (HTTP + Multiplex Demux + PTY)"] C1 --> Pool C2 --> Pool Pool --> WS Pool --> Sched Pool --> Sock end subgraph Docker["Linux Docker Engine"] K1["Container ws-a1b2
--network=none · --cap-drop=ALL
ws:rw · skills:ro · cgroups"] K2["Container ws-c3d4
--network=none · --cap-drop=ALL
ws:rw · skills:ro · cgroups"] end Sock --> K1 Sock --> K2 ``` ## Key Features - **User-Agnostic Workspace Isolation**: Keyed solely by `workspaceId = sha256(realpath(workspaceRoot))`. Works identically in vanilla DSH (single `Context`) and multi-context cloud Host servers (multiple isolated `Context` instances sharing one host-level `DockerRuntimePool`). - **Safe User Skill Execution**: Mounts `workspaceRoot` (`:rw` or `:ro`) and Skill directories strictly read-only (`:ro`). Never exposes sibling workspaces, `runtime/` databases, or host secrets (`KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN`, `DSH_*`). - **Two-Tier Cloud Concurrency & Fair Queuing**: - **Container pool (`maxActiveContainers`)** with automatic **LRU eviction** of idle containers and idle TTL reaping (`idleTtlMs`); - **Task pool (`maxConcurrentTasks` + `maxConcurrencyPerWorkspace`)** with **Per-Workspace Round-Robin Fair Queue** so one noisy workspace cannot starve others; - **Separate PTY terminal quota** so idle terminals never block short exec tasks; - Full `AbortSignal` queue cancellation, `maxQueueSize` fast-fail, `queueTimeoutMs`, and live observability metrics. - **Hardened Linux Defaults**: `CapDrop: ['ALL']`, `no-new-privileges:true`, `ReadonlyRootfs: true`, bounded `/tmp` tmpfs, non-root `User`, CPU/memory/PIDs cgroup caps, `NetworkMode: 'none'` by default, and optional OCI runtime (`runsc` / gVisor). - **Latest DSH Compatibility**: Peer-compatible with `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.1-rc.2` (including `0.2.2-rc.5` and `0.2.3-alpha`). ## Quick Start ### 1. Install the DSH Plugin Bundle `dsh-cloud-sandbox` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` (`./cordis.patch.yml`), icon, and localized metadata, so it can be installed directly via DSH's Plugin Manager UI or `dsh plugin add ` (after running `pnpm run build` for local checkouts). Enter the npm package name `dsh-cloud-sandbox` in the Plugin Manager, or install the precompiled package from the CLI: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-cloud-sandbox ``` For Web, replace `desktop` with `web`. To pin a version, enter `dsh-cloud-sandbox@0.2.3` in the Plugin Manager, or run: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-cloud-sandbox@0.2.3 ``` GitHub Releases also provide precompiled `dsh-cloud-sandbox-.tgz` assets; the Plugin Manager accepts their download URLs. Git installation through the former `dist` branch and `dist-v*` tags is no longer supported; use the npm package or a Release archive instead. `main` and source `v*` tags omit `dist/` and cannot be installed directly. Build the sandbox Docker image separately. Start Docker first: use Linux containers in Windows Docker Desktop, or start the relevant Docker Engine on Linux/WSL2. After installing the plugin, build the image below before using the sandbox. - **Local Desktop / Web mode (default)**: Automatically trusts workspaces registered in DSH's `workspaceRegistry`, mounts existing user Skill directories (`~/.agents/skills`, `~/.dsh/skills`) read-only, enables `networkMode: bridge` for runtime `pip3`/`npm` installs, stages uploaded session attachments into `/.dsh-uploads/`, and exposes the user-approval-gated `sandbox_import_file` tool (protected by `ctx.approval` + sensitive/credential path denylists) for importing specific host files as safe copies. - **Multi-Tenant Cloud lockdown (`DSH_SANDBOX_CLOUD_MODE=1`)**: Disables `trustRegisteredWorkspaces`, `mountUserSkills`, `allowApprovedHostReadOnly`, and `sandbox_import_file`, defaults `networkMode` to `'none'`, and keeps strict static `allowedBaseDirs` + per-session isolated attachment staging into `/.dsh-uploads/`. For cloud deployments that need public Internet access (while blocking LAN, cloud metadata `169.254.169.254`, host ports, and container-to-container traffic), run `sudo bash deploy/setup-public-egress-network.sh` (see [`deploy/README.md`](./deploy/README.md)) and set `DSH_SANDBOX_NETWORK_MODE=dsh-sandbox-public`. - **Environment variables**: `DSH_SANDBOX_IMAGE`, `DSH_SANDBOX_TRANSPORT`, `DSH_SANDBOX_LIFECYCLE`, `DSH_SANDBOX_ALLOWED_DIRS` (comma-separated), `DSH_SANDBOX_RO_MOUNTS` (comma-separated), `DSH_SANDBOX_NETWORK_MODE` (defaults to `bridge` locally and `none` when `DSH_SANDBOX_CLOUD_MODE=1`; set `dsh-sandbox-public` for No-LAN cloud public egress), `DSH_SANDBOX_CLOUD_MODE=1`, `DSH_SANDBOX_HOST_IMPORT=0`. ### 2. Build the Sandbox Image from the Installed Package The last build argument must name the directory containing `Dockerfile`. The installed package includes it, so the following commands work from any current directory. **Windows Desktop — CMD:** ```cmd docker build -t dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-cloud-sandbox" ``` **Windows Desktop — PowerShell:** ```powershell docker build -t dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-cloud-sandbox" ``` **DSH Web running inside Linux / WSL2 — Bash:** ```bash docker build -t dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-cloud-sandbox" ``` These paths use the default DSH home and profiles: `desktop` for Desktop and `web` for Web. Replace the profile directory when using another profile. On Windows with a custom `DSH_HOME`, replace `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` or `$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh` with that directory. Confirm the selected directory contains `Dockerfile`. When Windows DSH connects to a Docker Engine inside WSL2, build in that distribution using the POSIX path mapped from the Windows plugin installation directory. Build against the same Docker Engine the plugin connects to. **Build the image from a source checkout:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/dengmuming/dsh-cloud-sandbox.git cd dsh-cloud-sandbox docker build -t dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest . ``` Use the trailing `.` only from the source directory containing `Dockerfile`; it means the current directory. If Docker reports `open Dockerfile: no such file or directory`, use the installed package path above or change to the source directory first. After building, verify that the image exists: ```bash docker image inspect dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest ``` Once this succeeds, enable the plugin in DSH. If activation previously failed, enable it again or restart DSH. ### 3. Standalone DSH Integration (Single Context) ```ts import { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis' import { DockerSubprocessRuntime, DockerShellExecutor, WorkspaceFencedFileSystem } from 'dsh-cloud-sandbox' const ctx = new Context() await ctx.plugin(DockerSubprocessRuntime, { image: 'dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest', workspace: { allowedBaseDirs: ['/srv/dsh/workspaces'], readOnlyMounts: ['/opt/dsh/skills'], pathMode: 'mirror', }, scheduler: { maxActiveContainers: 20, maxConcurrentTasks: 12, maxConcurrencyPerWorkspace: 3, maxQueueSize: 100, queueTimeoutMs: 60_000, idleTtlMs: 15 * 60_000, }, security: { networkMode: 'none', cpus: 2, memoryBytes: 2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024, pidsLimit: 256, }, }) // Optional: enforce ctx.sandboxPolicy without danger-full-access escalation await ctx.plugin(DockerShellExecutor, { allowDangerFullAccess: false }) // Optional (for vanilla DSH without custom UserFileSystem): strict read+write workspace fence await ctx.plugin(WorkspaceFencedFileSystem, { allowedBaseDirs: ['/srv/dsh/workspaces'], readOnlyMounts: ['/opt/dsh/skills'], }) ``` ### 4. Multi-Context Cloud Host Integration Share **one** host-level `DockerRuntimePool` across every isolated Cordis `Context` so concurrency limits and fair queuing operate globally across the Linux host while keeping this plugin 100% user-agnostic: ```ts import { createDockerRuntimePool, DockerSubprocessRuntime, DockerShellExecutor } from 'dsh-cloud-sandbox' // Once at Host startup (root level): const dockerPool = createDockerRuntimePool({ image: 'dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest', workspace: { allowedBaseDirs: ['/var/lib/dsh/workspaces'], pathMode: 'mirror', // Dynamically mount only that workspace's associated skills directory as :ro resolveReadOnlyMounts: (workspaceRoot) => { // e.g. map /var/lib/dsh/workspaces/ -> associated read-only skills directory return [/* validated absolute path to skills dir */] }, }, scheduler: { maxActiveContainers: 32, maxConcurrentTasks: 16, maxConcurrencyPerWorkspace: 2, maxQueueSize: 128, queueTimeoutMs: 120_000, }, }) await dockerPool.initialize() // Inside each isolated Cordis Context: await ctx.plugin(DockerSubprocessRuntime, { pool: dockerPool, ownPool: false }) await ctx.plugin(DockerShellExecutor, { allowDangerFullAccess: false }) ``` ## Windows + WSL2 Support `dsh-cloud-sandbox` supports all three Windows/WSL2 setups with zero external dependencies: 1. **Running DSH inside WSL2 Linux**: Works identically to native Linux via `/var/run/docker.sock`. 2. **Running DSH natively on Windows with Docker Desktop (WSL2 backend)**: `transport: 'auto'` (or `'npipe'`) connects directly to `\\.\pipe\docker_engine`, translates Windows drive paths (`D:\work\ws1`) and WSL UNC paths (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...`) into POSIX container paths (`/mnt/d/work/ws1`), and uses structured `HostConfig.Mounts` to avoid drive-letter colon ambiguity. 3. **Running DSH natively on Windows with Docker Engine inside WSL2 (no Docker Desktop)**: Set `transport: 'wsl'` (or configure `wsl: { distro: 'Ubuntu-24.04' }`, or rely on `transport: 'auto'` fallback). The plugin bridges `node:http` directly to `/var/run/docker.sock` inside WSL2 over `wsl.exe` (`socat` → `python3` → `node` auto-fallback) with no open TCP ports: ```ts const dockerPool = createDockerRuntimePool({ image: 'dsh-cloud-sandbox-runtime:latest', transport: 'wsl', wsl: { distro: 'Ubuntu-24.04', // optional: omit for default WSL2 distro socketPath: '/var/run/docker.sock', mountPrefix: '/mnt', }, workspace: { allowedBaseDirs: ['D:\\workspaces'], readOnlyMounts: ['D:\\skills'], }, }) await dockerPool.initialize() ``` ## Development & Verification ```bash pnpm install pnpm run check # typecheck + vitest + build ``` ### GitHub Actions Releases Branch pushes and pull requests run `pnpm run check`. To release, update `package.json` and CHANGELOG, commit to `main`, then push a `v` tag matching the package version exactly: ```bash git tag v git push origin v ``` The Release workflow checks out that tag, installs locked dependencies, runs all checks, verifies the packed entry points and assets, and uploads the `.tgz` to its GitHub Release. With npm trusted publishing configured, it publishes the same archive to npm. Only the newest stable version among published GitHub Releases can become `latest` and run the npm job; retries of that version remain eligible, while prereleases and older versions do not replace it. To retry with the current workflow, use Actions → Release → Run workflow from `main` and enter the existing source tag. The workflow declares `contents: write` for Release uploads; broader default token permissions are unnecessary. See [publishing setup](./docs/publishing.md). ## Documentation - [Publishing and marketplace submissions](https://github.com/dengmuming/dsh-cloud-sandbox/blob/main/docs/publishing.md) — npm publishing identity, automation, and community index entries - [README.zh.md](./README.zh.md) — 简体中文文档 - [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) — Engineering invariants, layout, and agent guidelines - [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) — Threat model, container hardening, and Skill vs. Plugin boundaries - [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) — Contributor workflow and PR checklist - [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) — Version history ## License Licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-connect-workbuddy

把本机登录的 WorkBuddy 模型（国内版与国际版）接入 DeepSeek Harness —— 每次刷新自动读取每个模型的积分倍率，逐模型开关图片输入，多账号可切换，并带每日签到与只读积分概览（卡片与输入框里的胶囊读数）。

English · 安装 · 工作原理 · 账号池 · 更新日志 · 问题反馈

一个独立的 [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle 插件。它把本机已登录的 WorkBuddy 账号（**国内版与国际版 WorkBuddy AI 均支持**）接到 DSH 的模型选择器，同时提供账号池、可勾选的模型管理，以及一套围绕积分的只读能力：**每次刷新按上游目录自动读取每个模型的积分倍率**（`x0.79` 这种，倍率完全由上游给出，插件不写死也不猜）、逐模型开关图片输入、多账号切换与账号池自动换号、每日签到、以及卡片与输入框里胶囊式的只读积分读数。**国内版与国际版是两个并行的供应商（`workbuddy` / `workbuddy-global`），可同时使用**；插件设置页以 tab 区分两者，方便统一管理。只需本机 WorkBuddy 的登录态，**或在浏览器里登录一次**即可。 ### 图标样式 在设置页的「能力」tab 最下方选择图标样式。默认是本插件自己的图标；另一个皮肤跟随主题的文字颜色。选择会立即应用到侧边栏、页头和面板，并保存在当前浏览器中；其他浏览器需要单独设置。 ## 风险提示 > **WorkBuddy 已开始限制非官方客户端请求。本项目不保证相关接口长期可用，上游一旦收紧限制，插件可能失效。请先阅读文末[「免责声明」](#免责声明)，自行评估账号风险。使用官方 WorkBuddy 客户端始终是最安全的选择。** 需要说明的是，这个插件的目的很普通：**省掉在 WorkBuddy 客户端和 DSH 之间来回切换的麻烦**。你已经在自己的机器上登录了 WorkBuddy，插件只是把那份已有的登录态接到 DSH 的模型选择器上，让你在写代码的地方直接用到它——不提供账号、不共享凭据、不绕过计费。每一次调用都消耗**你自己账号**的额度，按上游给出的倍率真实扣费，插件从不修改账号状态，也不附带任何提权或刷额度的能力。 它依赖的是 WorkBuddy 客户端自身的接口（非官方开放 API），所以上游调整时插件可能需要跟着调整——这是这类工具的常态，也是这条提示存在的原因。**请自行评估账号风险后再决定是否安装。** ## 功能特性 - **配置在「设置 → WorkBuddy」** —— 设置面板左侧导航里与「账号与余额 / 通用设置 / 模型 / 插件」并列的一页。5.19.0 起**插件市场里那个 bundle 详情页不再显示配置卡片**：同一份配置只留这一个编辑入口。页面顶部是图标、标题与一句话简介，往下依次是国内版 / 国际版两个 tab、五个分栏，以及各自的保存与放弃。 - **双供应商并行接入（国内版 + 国际版）** —— 国内版注册为 `workbuddy` provider（`GLM-5.3`、`DeepSeek-V4-Pro`、`Kimi-K3`、`MiniMax-M3`、`Hy3` 等），国际版注册为 `workbuddy-global` provider（`GPT-5.6`、`Gemini-3.5-Flash`、`GLM-5.3`、`Kimi-K3` 等）。**有账号的区域其模型会出现在 DSH 模型选择器里**：两边都有账号时两组同时可选，不同会话可以各选一边，互不干扰。**本机没有账号的区域不列出任何模型**（该区域一个请求也发不出去，列出来只会点到就失败）；只要在该区域登录一次，「重新检测账号」或重启后模型就会自动出现——provider 本身始终注册着，因为它的设置页正是登录的入口（重新检测在账号池区块里）。模型名内嵌上游积分倍率（如 `GLM-5.3 · x0.79`），与 WorkBuddy 自身模型菜单一致；**活动时段显示的是折后价**——「夜间折扣」开着的时候，卡片与选择器上的数字一起变成 `x0.06`，活动一过自动回到原价，不需要重启（#120）。 - **设置页 tab 切换** —— 设置页顶部为「国内版 / 国际版」两个 tab，各含独立的账号池与模型管理；每个 tab 的账号、目录、勾选与未保存草稿完全隔离——在一个 tab 里切账号或刷新模型，不会触碰另一边的运行时目录与会话。 - **可单独关闭任一版本供应商** —— 每个 tab 右侧有一个勾选框（默认都勾选）。**取消勾选即把该供应商从 DSH 模型选择器里彻底撤掉**（不是只藏起 tab）：它的路由与「设置 → 模型」页的目录条目一并摘除，启动时也不再为它发无用请求。账号、积分、目录与勾选**全部保留**，重新勾选即完整恢复。典型用法是「我根本用不到国际版」——关掉它，让选择器干净。注意：若某会话此前选中的正是被关闭供应商的模型，该会话再调用会报 `NO_ADAPTER`，卡片会在关闭态的 tab 上明确提示这一点，不会静默失败。 - **设置页分栏：账号 / 模型 / 能力 / 诊断** —— 原来这一页是一列 3000 多像素的长页，把两类互不相干的事情混排在一起：**运维账号**（谁在服务、还剩多少、切换顺序、签到日志）与**编辑目录**（勾模型、上下文预算、推理档、关闭思考）。它们连提交语义都不同——账号改动点一下即生效，目录改动是草稿、必须点保存——所以「保存」按钮常常离它要保存的东西隔着三屏。现在分栏，一栏只做一件事；**切栏既不会重新拉取，也不会丢掉未保存的目录草稿**（非活动栏留在页面里，只是通过 `hidden` 不可见，因此也不进入无障碍树）。第三栏「能力」放的是**授权类开关**——允许调用本机 CodeBuddy CLI、允许模型自主生图、积分读数显示在哪——它们点一下即生效、从不经过保存，而且每一个都留着长自己子选项的位置（CLI 的工作目录、生图的尺寸或价格上限），所以不挤在账号表格上方那一小条里。第四栏「诊断」是只读的事实表：当前区域、上游域名、真正在服务的账号名、登录有效期、目录里共几个模型、启用了几个、账号池开关，以及上游最近一次错误的**原文**（原样引用，不翻译、不概括）——这一栏存在的唯一理由就是能被整段贴进问题反馈，所以里面没有任何会改设置的控件。 - **刷新频率（`pollIntervalMs`，默认 5 分钟）** —— 卡片多久重读一次账号表。**这是一次真实的请求量决定**：每次刷新要为池内每个账号各读一次积分（`/v2/billing/meter/get-user-resource`）和一次签到状态（`/v2/billing/meter/checkin-activity-status`），所以 4 个账号的池子按旧的固定 60 秒算，一天约 11,520 个请求——而这些数字本来动得很慢。默认改成 **5 分钟**（约为原来的 1/5），「能力」栏给五档：1 / 5 / 10 / 30 / 60 分钟，点一下即生效、不走保存。**输入框的账号面板跟随同一个值**：此前它自己写死 60 秒，只是「碰巧」等于卡片的 60 秒，两边一旦改动就会对同一个账号给出不同说法（面板还画着「模型繁忙」、卡片已经说恢复正常）——现在只有一个间隔，改一处两处一起变。**取值是封闭的五档**：配置文件里手写的 `0` 或别的数字一律回落到默认值，因为「不刷新」和「疯狂刷新」都不是用户想要的，而这个数字直接驱动 `setInterval`。 - **可选：侧边栏入口（`sidebarPanel`，默认关闭）** —— 在 DSH 侧边栏加一行 WorkBuddy，点开就是**这张卡片的整页版**（左上有「返回会话」）。分栏挤在设置面板那 800px 里时，账号表格、模型目录与诊断原文都只有半屏宽；整页版把同一批东西摊到整栏。**默认关闭**：这一行占的是**所有已安装插件共用的全局侧边栏座位**，而「设置 → WorkBuddy」本来就能打开同一页，一次升级不该替用户占这个位置。开关在「能力」栏，**勾上即出现、取消即消失，不走保存**——与这一栏其它授权类开关一致。 - **关掉时是把注册注销，不是渲染空组件**：侧边栏导航行是用槽位**条目元数据**（`label` + 图标）拼的，组件返回 `null` 只会得到一颗**空白但仍可点**的按钮。所以决策点在 `apply`（`src/client/panel-switch.ts` 是卡片与入口之间的接缝），关掉即 `dispose`。 - **首屏状态问宿主，不问浏览器里的设置镜像**：那份镜像在部分 0.1.7 上是陈的，且只在命名空间**边缘**触发、不在**值变化**时触发——一份陈的 `false` 会让这一行整个会话都不出现，且没有任何事件来纠正它。所以种子读宿主自己的答案（usage 文档的 `sidebarPanelEnabled`）。 - **开着面板时关掉，中间栏自己回对话**（`ui-layout` 丢掉已不存在的 `activePanelId`），不需要插件去导航。macOS 实测记录见 [docs/MAC-VERIFY-PR188-REPORT.md](docs/MAC-VERIFY-PR188-REPORT.md)，验证清单见 [docs/MAC-VERIFY-PR188.md](docs/MAC-VERIFY-PR188.md)。 - **模型管理** —— 从上游刷新完整模型目录，逐项勾选启用或禁用；**勾选是草稿，点保存才生效**（issue 23:00–7:50」）。**徽标是「此刻」的函数**：活动只在它自己声明的时间窗内显示，窗口一关徽标就自己消失；跨零点的时段按上游声明的时区判断；同一个模型命中多条活动时只画优先级最高的那条。上游没给结束时间的权益标记（如「订阅优先」）则常驻，直到上游把它下架。**徽标只是提示，不改变模型行为**——它标注的是上游此刻给出的活动与折扣，不替你做选择。**同一枚徽标也出现在 DSH 个模型、**没有任何负载/排队字段**。这不是本插件没实现，也不是配置或权限问题：**上游国际版从未提供这个数据**。所以国际版只显示模型名与活动徽标，探针那条请求失败后安静退化成「没有徽标」，不会挡住模型列表，也不会用延迟或积分去猜一个「忙不忙」。 - **排队时说清楚你排在第几位** —— 上游用三个业务码表达排队（`6020` 等待、`6021` 队列满、`6022` **模型可用性测试（含冷却恢复时间）** —— 限量模型的冷却时间过去只能靠反复试错去猜。现在每个模型行有一个「测试」按钮，直接告诉你它此刻能否使用、不能用时何时恢复。**它发的是一条真实体积的请求（约 25k 输入 token）**，而不是「发个 ping 看通不通」——因为上游的限流**按请求体积触发**（实测约 20k 能过、约 30k 被拒），小请求看着正常、长对话里却可能每次都被拒，那正是「测试通过、实际被限」的来源。**恢复时间的来源**：上游的 429 **不带** `Retry-After` 响应头（也没有 `X-RateLimit-*`），但它把重置时间写在**响应体**里——`{"code":6004,"msg":"…将在 2026-09-30 02:30:30 UTC+8 `Retry-After`，值是账号月度积分包的刷新时刻（实测 `2026-11-01 00:00 +08:00`），它不是「你在此之前不能用」——所以成功的行只显示「✓ 可用」，绝不附「之后可再用」；旧版本已经写进文件的那类记录会在读取时自动治愈。探测在后台发起，**凭据不会传到页面**；结果不写入设置，也不改变你已保存的勾选。 **两点需要知道**：① **它真的花钱**——实测一次报 `credit` 0.02（被限流时直接 429，几乎不花）。因此**只能按单个模型手工点**，没有「测试已勾选」这类批量按钮：一次覆盖整个列表就是一次不可控支出（服务端也据此**只接受单个模型**，多模型请求会被拒）。② 上游虽宣称 1M 上下文，但节流线远低于此；插件按模型的**原生窗口**向 DSH 宣称（3.5.0 起不再默认压到 200K），所以 DSH 拿到的正是它；「模型原生窗口」这一档对应的是**没有上限**，选中它会把这个模型的预算条目删掉，而不是写一个恰好等于窗口的数字——这样上游日后调大该模型的窗口时，这一档会跟着变大。 - **生图工具 `workbuddy_draw_image`（国内版 / 国际版，默认关闭，逐区授权）** —— 把 WorkBuddy 的文生图能力交给 3.2M，照着算和照着抄得到两个不同答案）：合法范围是两边各 512–2560 像素、宽乘高不超过约 419 万像素（2026-10-25 逐档实测：`1024x1536` / `2048x2048` / `2048x1536` / `2560x1440` / `2560x1600` 都成功且输出宽高与请求一致；`2560x2560` 起被直接拒绝），**越界不再报错**——`fitIntoRange()` 会按「`2560/长边`」与「`√(4194304/面积)`」中更小的比例等比缩/放后照常出图，并在 `hint` 里写明「按你给的 X 缩放成 WxH」，同时用 `requestedSize` 回带你原本写的值（写 `auto` 时就是 `auto`），所以「用户要 4K、实际出 2560x1440 档」这件事可以被程序识别、不必正则抠散文（`4K` 在描述里不设独立档：横竖方分别与 2K 同档，因为工具上限是**单边 2560、面积 4,194,304**，写不出真 4K——上限只能用这一组数说，`2048x2048` 才是顶格的那一档）。`region` 与 `size` 都在输出的 `required` 里（两个都由工具自己算，一定在），想按区记账或按尺寸做后处理直接读字段即可。**改图（带 `image`）推荐直接写 `size: "auto"`**：工具会从图片字节里解出第一张的宽高（PNG / JPEG / GIF / WEBP），按同比例给一个长边 1024–1536 的画布（`1600x900` → `1536x864`），模型看不到原图也不必猜比例——只有比对 5:1 auto」等于先用掉一次积分再问——现在的写法是「先说一句会按这个比例裁切/留白、原版式可能被切，他同意再调」。本地因此只剩一种尺寸失败：比例极端到缩不出合法值（`INVALID_ARGS`，不扣积分）。再大只能走超分，单纯调参数已经到顶。**它真的花钱**，所以工具描述第二段就把价目写出来——国内版约 5.71 积分/张、国际版约 0.03 积分/张（同一计量单位、相差约 190 倍），模型和你开局就知道这一张多少钱，并且知道「走哪个区这一次改不了、也查不到，只能以返回的 `region` 为准」（所以描述里不要求模型在调用前报价，只要求如实报两个区、并点明差约 190 倍）；真实扣费仍以返回的 `credit` 为准，结果里同时写明**这次走的是国内版还是国际版**、用的哪个模型、实际扣了多少积分（区域从凭据 domain 现算，两区都开着时优先国内版）。描述里不点名具体模型 id，免得模型主动去猜——`model` 一般留空最稳；失败后有 30 秒冷却（但参数写错、没登录、模型不存在这三类一分钱没花，不进冷却），也不提供「一次画四张」这类不可控支出的参数。工具定义是手写的 raw JSON Schema，**没有引入任何新依赖**。第十九轮又收了三处「同一件事两个口径」：① 尺寸链的入口加了**主体门禁**——主体没问清之前整条链一条都不许走（旧稿 (a) 让他先问「想画什么」、第 2 阶又已经把 `2560x1440` 填好，「随便画个 `16:9` 的」于是自编主体扣一次费）；② 用途表补了**方行遇方向**那一支（配图是方行，旧稿只写「横行要竖」「竖行要横」，「给这篇文章配张图，要横的」无定义、会填 `1024x1024` 与同段例子 `1536x1024` `credit`」收紧成「**本次调用**拿到过」——190 倍差正是跨区、跨模型产生的，拿上一次的单价报这一次等于报错价。第二十、二十一轮又收了三处**同一事实两个出口**：① 用户说「我这张是 1600x900」时，① 的触发词（数字 + x）会先吞掉它、脚注又说该写 `auto`——现在第 4 阶第一句先分类「这是输出尺寸还是输入图尺寸」，输入尺寸永远不填进 `size`；② 主体例子原来「秋季新品静物」是正例、「秋季新品」是反例，而用户原话正是后者，现在换成「一束向日葵」。第二十二轮又收掉三处「照字面执行必然出错」：① **4K 不再既算档位词又算「做不到」**——七条第 5 条原来写「用户要的东西本工具做不到（真 4K…）」要先停，第 3 阶又让「照 2K 填、出完再说明」直接调，同一句「来张 4K 壁纸」两个出口；现在清单里只留「明确要 `3840x2160` 24fps 帧数为准（请求 5 秒得 5.09–5.17 秒）。取证、协议与联调记录见 [docs/VIDEO_GEN.md](docs/VIDEO_GEN.md)。 - **本机账号切换** —— 自动发现 WorkBuddy 桌面端留下的多个登录凭据，可按区域切换账号；Token 不写入 DSH 设置。 - **对话输入框积分读数（国内版 / 国际版自动切换）** —— 次也救不了）：成功一轮、或你自己发一条消息，计数清零；插件自己发的不清零。子代理会话一律不碰；会话正在跑、或收件箱已有排队内容时也不发。**每次都会真实消耗一次请求**，所以默认关闭；它也是本插件里**唯一一个改完即生效**的上游类开关。与其它上游开关一样，也能直接在 `cordis.patch.yml` 里写： ```yaml channelRejectContinue: enabled: true maxConsecutive: 1 text: 继续 ``` - **凭据失效时给出可执行的建议** —— 上游拒绝当前账号的 token 时，插件会**实际探测**本机其他账号：若有账号仍然可用，就直接告诉你「切换到它即可」（并附一键切换），而不是笼统地让你重新登录——被钉在一个作废的旧备份上时，重新登录并不能解决问题。只有本机确实没有别的账号可切换时，才会提示重新登录。 - 虽同样加密，插件**不读取也不显示**。若 App 安装在非常规位置，用 `WORKBUDDY_APP_EXECUTABLE` 指定其可执行文件。 ## 公司网络连不上 CN 网关？ 如果插件在某个网络里**全部模型都超时**，而同一台机器上的 WorkBuddy 桌面客户端**正常**，那多半是网关按 **TLS SNI** 被拦了：`copilot.tencent.com` --profile desktop exec dsh-connect-workbuddy doctor` ## 账号池

一台机器上往往登录过多个 WorkBuddy 账号。**账号池**把这件事收成一次点击：把要用的账号勾进池子，然后「签到勾选的账号」或「测试勾选的账号」；再打开**启用账号池**，插件就会在请求失败时自动换号接着跑。 **每个区域（国内版 / 国际版）各有独立的一池**：成员与目标模型互不影响——两边的账号本来就属于不同的上游栈。**签到只有国内版有**：海外区域不显示签到按钮，也没有那一列。 > **窄栏下这张表会变成堆叠卡片。** 配置页住在设置面板里，内容列只有 **564px**（800px 面板减去 188px 导航）——五列表格塞不进去，所以窗口宽度小于 700px（量的是**表格自己**的宽度，不是视口）时，每一行改成三行：账号与操作各占一行，中间三个事实共享一行。窄栏下实测单行 **96px**（此前 157px，账号名被压成「用户75」），账号名不再截断。宽栏形态一行未改。 ### 自动换号（开启账号池即生效） - **谁来服务由排序决定**：开启账号池后，**每一次请求**都发给池子里排序最靠前的可用账号——所以「当前使用」显示的是排序的结果，不一定是你手动选的那个。排序规则见下一节。 - **失败时继续往下试**：某个请求在上游失败时，插件会**依次**用池内其他可用账号重试，直到有一个接手、或全部不可用为止；全部失败才把错误报出来（并在错误里注明尝试过几个账号）。 - **哪些失败会换号**：429 限流、402 无积分、401 凭据失效、502 网关/网络——这些都是**某个账号**的状态，换一个账号很可能就过了。 - **哪些不会**：请求本身不合法（HTTP 400）。同一个请求体换哪个账号都是同样的 400，重试只是让用户多等几轮才看到同一个错误。**流中途断开也不会重试**——字节已经发出去了，重放会让客户端看到两段拼接的回答。 - **已知不可用的账号会被跳过**：正在限流冷却期内、或凭据已被上游拒绝的成员不会参与（这也是「一键测试」的意义：测试结果直接决定谁能被选中）。**从没测试过的账号按「默认可用」参与**——刚发现的登录不该因为「还没测」就被排除。 - **手动选择不会被改写**：池子通过运行时覆盖决定「谁服务」，**从不写回你保存的选择**；关闭账号池，你选定的账号立刻完全恢复生效。这也是为什么卡片要显示「当前使用」——它可能不是你在上面选的那个，而你应该看得出来。 - **失败会被记下来**：某个请求撞上失败时，插件把这次失败写成该账号的测量（含上游报文里给出的重置时间），所以**下一个请求直接从可用账号开始**，不会每次都先撞一遍同一个限流账号。只有需要你手动「一键测试」时才不写测量这件事，从此不成立了。HTTP 400 例外——那是**请求**不合法，与账号无关，记下来会白白闲置一个好账号；未勾选进池的账号也不记（勾选才是「可以花它的积分」的同意）。 - 每次换号都会在宿主日志里留一行 `warn`，写明因何失败、换到了下一个账号。 ### 这个开关到底控制什么 **它只控制「插件要不要自己决定」，不控制「你能不能操作」。** | | 账号池 **开启** | 账号池 **关闭** | |---|---|---| | 谁服务 | 由排序**自动**选出（可用优先 → 快过期先花 → 积分高 → 凭据新） | **你在账号池里手动选**「使用哪个账号」 | | 请求失败 | **自动**换下一个可用账号重试 | 不换号，如实报错 | | 一键签到 / 一键测试 | 可用 | **仍然可用** | | 目标测试模型 | 可改 | **仍然可改** | 最后两行是刻意的：签到与测试是**手动动作**，它们作用于你勾选的成员，与「插件是否自动路由」是两件事。之前把按钮也挂在开关上，导致关掉账号池就**再也没法签到或测试**——而「关闭」本该是「我手动来」，不是「什么都不许做」。 **手动选择账号在哪里**：账号池区块里。**关闭账号池时**，该区块会显示一行「使用哪个账号」的下拉，选定即生效（写回本区域的账号槽，与凭据失效时的「切换到可用账号」走同一条已验证的写入路径）；**开启账号池时这一行不显示**——那时由排序决定，一个改了不生效的下拉比没有更糟。账号的发现（「重新检测账号」）、勾选、签到与测试全部集中在这个区块里，所以账号管理只有一处。 **唯一的硬约束**：池里一个成员都没勾选时，批量动作一律拒绝。空的池**绝不**退化成「那就对全部账号执行」——那是唯一会花掉你没授权过的积分的解读。 ### 排序规则（开启账号池后决定谁服务） 1. **可用优先** —— 被测量判定为不可用（限流未到恢复时间、凭据被拒、连通性失败等）的排到最后，不参与选择； 2. **快过期的积分先花** —— 3 天内到期的积分用不掉就作废，所以**有临期积分的账号排在前面**，**先到期的先排**；两个都在临期时，**临期积分多的优先**； 3. **积分高者优先** —— 在没有临期积分的账号里，选积分最多的。**积分只在有新鲜读数时参与**（卡片轮询、批量测试或保存时读到的那份，10 分钟内有效）：普通选号只读取缓存；独立的限频恢复查询只核对已记录积分耗尽的成员； 4. **凭据更晚过期的优先**； 5. 最后按账号 id 收尾，保证顺序是**全序**、可复现，不会因为账号表顺序变化而抖动。 > **第 2 条为什么排到第 3 条前面**（issue #70）：这两条此前是**严格字典序**——先比积分总量，只有总量**完全相等**才比到期时间。而总量几乎从不恰好相等，于是「快过期优先」**实际上从未生效过**：一条「不花就作废」的规则被另一条完全遮蔽，等于死代码。真实病例里，某账号有 **196.4 分当天作废**，只因为比另两个账号少约 1,200 分就永远排在最后，那 196 分必然烂掉。 > > 代价也要说清：这条规则会让**临期 1 分**的账号排到**余额 5 万**的账号前面。这不是缺陷——积分是通用的，不花那 1 分它**确定**会损失；而余额 5 万的账号下一轮还在。唯一的真实代价是临期账号可能不够跑完一个请求，这时由既有的换号逻辑接手。 ### 两个批量动作 - **签到勾选的账号** —— 逐个账号签到。**签到前先查当天状态**，已签到的直接标记为「已签到」而**不发写入请求**（幂等，不重复领取）；任何单个账号失败只标记该行，**不中断整批**。 - **测试勾选的账号** —— 对每个成员发一次**真实体积**的探测请求（约 25k 输入 token；与模型行的「测试」是同一套 `probeModel`，因而同样继承两个实测结论：限流**按请求体积**触发、恢复时间写在**响应体**里而不是响应头），得出该账号此刻能否用这个模型。 **测试目标是哪个模型**：默认是**该区域目录里倍率为 0 的免费模型**（实测国内版当前只有 `hy3` 一个；**不写死名字**，因为上游会改倍率——`deepseek-v4.1-flash` 就已从 0 变成 0.11），也可以在下拉里指定一个具体模型。指定的模型若已离开目录，**手动动作会明确拒绝**（`target-model-stale`），而不是偷偷换一个——你点的是「测这个模型」，换掉就是答非所问。 **成本与边界**：测试是真实请求，指向免费模型时（倍率 0）几乎不花钱，但它**不是零成本的空转**；签到则会真实领取当日奖励。默认两个动作都**只在你点按钮时执行**；自动签到是一个**显式的、默认关闭**的开关，打开它才是你授权插件替你领——它先读状态，已签到的不重复领取。 ### 池成员是显式勾选，默认一个都不含 「本机有登录」不等于「要拿它去签到和花积分」。成员默认**空**，必须逐个勾选（或点「全选」）；**空池不会退化成「全部账号」**——没勾选时两个批量动作直接拒绝，而不是替你把所有账号跑一遍。 勾选是一次**草稿编辑**：点「保存」才落盘，未保存时保存按钮带 dirty 指示；切走或关掉卡片，草稿仍在。 ### 手动选择：卡片上没有账号下拉了 账号**一律在账号池里管**：成员勾选就是现在的账号选择面，「重新检测账号」也在那一块。原先那个「账号选择」下拉在有账号池之后是自相矛盾的——池开启时由排序决定谁服务，它改什么都不生效，却看起来像权威；顶部状态行还可能显示成 A、下拉显示成 B。 所以区域状态行也跟着改：**池开启时不再报出某一个账号名**（多个账号同时登录是常态，用单数说「已登录：A」本身就是错的），只陈述本区域可用、由池决定用谁；**池关闭时才报出那个账号**——那时它确实是唯一答案。状态行旁边的圆点与 token 过期时间讲的是「这个区域能不能用」，和「谁在计费」是两件事，后者由账号池区块负责显示。 ### 账号为什么出池，以及什么时候回来 | 探测结果 | 对轮换的意义 | | --- | --- | | 可用 | 可入选 | | 被限流 | **暂时**出池，按上游给出的重置时间自动回池（上游没说时间就按 30 分钟兜底，**不编造倒计时**） | | 积分耗尽 | 出池，后续正余额查询确认到账后回池；月度刷新时间不作为恢复倒计时 | | 连不上上游 / 失败 | **暂时**出池，30 分钟后自动回池——这类结果说的往往不是账号，而是一次网络抖动或上游 5xx | | 凭据被拒 / 模型不存在 | 出池，**只能靠手动「测试」回池**：一个需要重新登录，一个是本区域不再提供该模型，等待都修不好 | | **账号被上游限制使用** | **停权，等待修不好**（5.8.0）。上游的话是「账号存在异常行为，已被限制使用」——它点名的是**这个账号**，所以自动换号**会**绕开它去用下一个。这与「渠道校验失败」正好相反：那条说的是**这个请求**，换号只会白烧一次额度，因此**不**换号。**回池的实际出路只有手动「测试」**：账号 id 是 `uin`/`uid` 的哈希，重新登录后仍是同一个 id，插件也不会因为重登清掉这条测量（「重新授权就回池」不成立）；上游解除限制后测一次通过，它才会重新成为候选。插件**不给它编一个倒计时**，但停权只作用于轮换候选资格——全池没有可用账号时，请求仍会落到你保存的那个账号上 | 关键一条：**「被限流」「连不上上游」都不等于不可用**。它们恰恰是最值得等的那两类状态——当成永久失效剔除，正好丢掉池子里本来最能用的账号，而且**
