Plugins for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Each one is an independent npm package, verified end to end against a real DSH host before release.
English · 中文


## Plugins

| Plugin                                                                                                                          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Version                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [**session-delete**](packages/session-delete#readme)
[screenshots](packages/session-delete/README.md#screenshots) | Really deletes sessions instead of just archiving them. Deleted sessions go to a restorable trash; the confirm dialog shows one line of impact (size · sub-sessions · running) and Enter executes it. Supports `⌘⌥⌫` for the current session, one-click clearing of a whole workspace, and chunked permanent deletion from the trash. Every action goes into an audit log, and a receipt lists anything left behind.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-session-delete?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-session-delete) |
| [**session-rewind**](packages/session-rewind#readme)                                                                            | Rewind a conversation in place: `Esc` `Esc` or the ↶ button next to Copy, then choose conversation-only or conversation-plus-files. Everything from the target message on is withdrawn from the model context and transcript; changed files are restored with pre-write snapshots, rescue points and a trash, and the message text/images return to the composer. A panel lists withdrawn messages, audit history, rescue points and diagnostics. The log is append-only. Bare `↑` / `↓` in the composer recalls prompts you already sent, without rewinding anything.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-session-rewind?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-session-rewind) |
| [**next-step**](packages/next-step#readme)                                                                                      | A decision card when a turn is worth continuing: a short summary of checkable facts, the question you need to settle, and 1–2 mutually exclusive next steps that name a concrete object and send exactly their own text with one click. How often it appears is a user-chosen tier (strict / balanced / eager); a withheld card is one click away and reveals the candidate already computed, with no second model call. A local review log (no message text, local only) plus a Wilson-interval report make the thresholds and wording tunable against evidence. Optionally (off by default) a grey ghost hint in the empty composer, accepted with `Tab` or `→`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-next-step?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-next-step)           |
| [**advisor**](packages/advisor#readme)                                                                                          | On-demand second opinion: the main model decides when to consult a separately configured advisor model, which reads the whole conversation — tool calls and results included — and returns structured advice. Advisory only — it never approves, blocks or runs anything. Off by default; shadow mode, four-level budgets and a token ledger keep the extra calls visible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-advisor?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-advisor)               |
| [**btw**](packages/btw#readme)                                                                                                  | Ask a read-only side question without interrupting the main task. The command fires mid-turn instead of queueing; the answer runs in a forked, tool-less child agent enforced by a runtime guard, so it never enters the conversation history. The fork reuses the parent prompt prefix (57–94% served from cache, no cache-write charge), and answers persist to a per-session history file. A tab in the native right sidebar streams answers as they are generated and renders full Markdown (the conversation narrows instead of being covered); threads support follow-up, promote-to-draft (Markdown source, insert only, never auto-send), and an honest scope badge.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-btw?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-btw)                       |
| [**artifacts**](packages/artifacts#readme)                                                                                      | Local artifact pages for a session: one `artifact` tool publishes a self-contained HTML page, a compact summary row lands in the timeline, and the latest version refreshes in place inside a sandboxed right-sidebar panel. Versions are files under the DSH data root; nothing is uploaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-artifacts?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-artifacts)           |
| [**projects**](packages/projects#readme)                                                                                        | Project-level context: sessions grouped into projects, with the project's standing rules and `MEMORY.md` index injected before every request (registered once, rendered per session). One panel shows threads, memory, audit and pending approvals. Threads get isolated Git worktrees with safe archiving; the coordinator proposes by default and has a tiny tool basket (no shell, file writes, deletion, push or merge) — dangerous actions can only be requested and need a switch on to execute. Remote writes are off by default and doubly gated: `git push`, `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge` each need a danger switch plus a human approval, and they use your own `git` / `gh` credentials.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-projects?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-projects)             |
| [**casefile**](packages/casefile#readme)
[screenshots](packages/casefile/README.md#workbench)                     | Evidence-first workbench for reverse-engineering investigations on top of REA: observations become citable evidence, claims that cite them, and obligations that close only against a fresh PASS check bound to the implementation digest. Runs real checks (`build` / `cli` / `web` screenshot similarity / `process` side effects / project self-test JSON), reopens a closed obligation the moment the implementation changes, and refuses to close a project until coverage, unknowns and check freshness all line up. Exports a redacted spec pack, an acceptance report (Markdown or a self-contained HTML archive) and a deterministic machine-readable bundle; supports L3 unattended runs gated to `scope=selected` with per-kind checks and budgets, plus ingesting external agents' reports under a stable contract (recorded, not endorsed). No MCP bridge, no analysis engine, no DRM bypass. | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-casefile?label=)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-casefile)             |
| More plugins are on the way.                                                                                                    |

## Install

**From Discover (recommended).** Open **Plugins → Discover → Add index source** in DSH and paste:

```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@kangyishuai/dsh-plugin-index/index.json
```

Every plugin in this repository then shows up with its description, category and version list, and can be installed with one click. The index is rebuilt from npm after every release, so it always lists the versions that actually exist.

**From the command line:**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kangyishuai/dsh-session-delete
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kangyishuai/dsh-session-rewind
```

Then restart the DSH desktop app. Each plugin's README covers usage, side effects and compatibility.

## How these plugins are built

- **Nothing destructive without a way back.** Deletion goes to a trash first. A confirm dialog states the impact: count, size, whether the session is live, and whether it can be undone. See [ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-destructive-operations.md).
- **No hard-coded internals.** DSH is pre-release and its on-disk formats change. Plugins scan and match known patterns, and leave anything they don't recognize alone.
- **Verified on a real host.** Unit tests, plus an end-to-end GUI smoke test against a throwaway DSH home. Compatibility tables say exactly which DSH version was checked.
- **No telemetry, no hidden calls.** Plugins never phone home, and they only touch the local DSH data directory as documented. Extra model calls are only these deliberate ones, all through the host's own LLM service and the provider you already configured: `advisor` (off by default) adds one call when the main model consults it; `next-step` (on by default) adds one call after a turn that ends normally to compute its decision card (its cheap gates skip some turns); `btw` and `projects` only add calls when you actually invoke them.
- **Plain JavaScript, no build step.** What you install is what's in the repo ([ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-plain-js-with-jsdoc.md)).

> **Disclaimer:** this is a personal community project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek. Plugins are young software, so keep backups of anything you can't lose.

## Contributing

Issues and PRs are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), which covers setup, commands, commit conventions and the release flow. Design notes live in [docs/](docs/README.md) (in Chinese).

## Security

Please report vulnerabilities privately. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# @kangyishuai/dsh-btw > **Read-only side questions that do not interrupt the main task.** [中文](./README.zh-CN.md) Unofficial plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Not affiliated with DeepSeek. ## What it does `/btw ` asks a side question about the current work **without interrupting the main task and without adding to the conversation history**. - **Available while the agent is working.** The command dispatches immediately instead of queueing behind the running turn (measured: 215 ms, no user message created). - **Read-only.** The side question runs in a forked child agent with **no tools**; a tool guard is armed on that child's own scope and denies any tool call from it, and `send_message` is always denied. - **Cheap.** The fork reuses the parent conversation's prompt prefix, so the provider serves most of it from cache (measured: 57% on the first fork, 94% on a repeat). Cache writes are not billed. - **Kept.** Answers are written to a per-session JSONL history so you can reopen the last one with a bare `/btw`. - **Threads.** Follow up on a side question without losing the earlier exchange; the thread's history is replayed to the model each turn. - **Streaming.** The drawer renders the answer as it is generated instead of waiting for the whole reply (the host buffers the child's text deltas; the panel reads them through `btw/live`). - **Markdown.** Headings, lists, tables, quotes, fenced code and inline styles render properly. The promote draft keeps its Markdown source, so it renders correctly once you send it. - **Readable numbers.** The cost badge adapts tokens to `K/M/B/T` and duration to `ms/s/m/h` (for example `new 12.3K · cached 988K · 32.5s`). - **Promote to draft.** Turn the **whole thread** into a four-section Markdown draft (first question / latest conclusion / key details including every follow-up / still unresolved) and **insert it into the composer — never send it**. You decide whether to send. - **Native right sidebar.** The「旁问」button opens a tab in the DSH right sidebar: the conversation becomes narrower but is **never covered**.the sidebar's own collapse button (⌥⌘B) collapses the column and clicking the「旁问」button expands it again. Hosts without the sidebar service fall back to a right-edge overlay drawer. - **Chat order.** Threads list oldest first with every turn expanded, the newest answer at the bottom, and the view follows the latest content. - **Honest scope badge.** The drawer states how many side questions exist and reminds you that **the model can see the whole conversation**; a scope choice only narrows the instruction, it does not cut context. ## How it works A third-party DSH plugin cannot reach a provider adapter through `ctx.llm` (every access path resolves to an instance without adapters). The supported path is a **forked subagent**: 1. `ctx.subagents.startActivation({ provider: 'fork', parent: agent, … })` — the parent `Agent` comes from the command invocation. 2. A `tools.guard(...)` is armed **on the child's own context** (`ctx.agents.get(childId).ctx.tools`) so the side question stays read-only. The host registers a guard in the calling scope and checks `[global, ...agent scope chain]`, so a guard armed through the child only constrains that side question (agent scopes have no parent link, so the chain is just that agent's own layer — nothing else inherits it). The plugin never arms one through its own unscoped context: that would land in the host's **global** layer and deny tool calls for **every** agent in the process while the side question runs. If the child context cannot be resolved, no guard is armed at all — the internal run result records `guardScope: "none"` (no RPC field or UI shows it) — and the prompt still forbids tool use. 3. The child's answer is read from the activation result, the child session is archived so it does not clutter the session list, and the Q&A is appended to history. Follow-ups re-fork each turn and replay the thread's own Q&A into the prompt — a fork is single-turn, so keeping one child alive would degenerate into a full side session with its own lifecycle. Live text never leaves the host process as raw history: an `llm/stream` observer keyed by the child session keeps at most 12k characters in memory, the panel polls `btw/live`, and the buffer is dropped when the run ends. The panel deliberately does not subscribe to the child session from the client: a forked child is seeded with the parent's completed transcript, so retaining it would download that whole history into the browser just to read the tail. Markdown is parsed on the host into a JSON block tree and the client only maps it to React elements — no HTML injection, no bundler, and no import of host UI packages. Promote only **returns text** from the host and inserts it with the composer's `setDraft`; `submit` is never called. If the composer already has content the action is refused instead of overwriting what you were typing. Scope is deliberately **advisory**: a fork inherits every completed turn of the parent, and a plugin cannot inherit a subset. The badge says so instead of pretending the context was trimmed. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kangyishuai/dsh-btw ``` Restart the DSH desktop app afterwards. ## Usage ``` /btw what was the name of that config file again? /btw # reopen the last answer /btw --thread # continue an existing thread /btw --scope recent # hint the answer to focus (session | recent | selection) ``` The panel opens from the「旁问」button left of the composer as a tab in the **native DSH right sidebar**: the conversation becomes narrower but the panel never covers it. Use the sidebar's own collapse button (⌥⌘B) to collapse the column (the tab is kept), and the「旁问」button to expand it again; close the tab with its own × or the panel's「关闭」button. Hosts that do not load the sidebar service fall back to a right-edge overlay drawer that collapses to a thin edge rail. Threads are listed oldest first with every turn expanded, and the newest answer is at the bottom — the view scrolls to the latest content when you open the drawer or when new content arrives. Each answer renders Markdown; a long answer is clamped with「Show all」. The composer at the bottom starts a new side question, while「Follow up」inside a thread opens that thread's own input. ## Configuration Plugin config (set when adding the plugin to a profile): | Key | Default | Meaning | | -------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `allowedTools` | `[]` | Tool names the side question may use. Empty means fully read-only. `send_message` is never allowed. | | `language` | `auto` | `en` / `zh`; `auto` follows the system locale. | | `dataRoot` | `$DSH_HOME` → `~/.dsh` | Where history and settings live (`/btw/`). | Runtime settings (editable in **Settings → Side questions**, stored in `/btw/settings.json`): | Key | Default | Meaning | | ---------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `allowedTools` | `[]` | Overrides the plugin config above when non-empty. | | `historyLimit` | `50` | Records kept per session (1–200). The plugin reads this value on every history read and write: lowering it hides older records immediately and physically trims the file on the next side question. | | `echoAnswer` | `true` | Also show the full answer in the conversation; off = panel only. | | `boundedContext` | `false` | Above 400K tokens of session context, use a spawn child with the last 12 messages instead of forking the whole session. Opt-in; answers may miss older context. | The settings file is re-read on every use, so edits take effect without restarting the host. Promotion inserts an **unsent draft** only; it never sends. The draft is fitted to the current composer width and capped at six lines: a short thread keeps the four-section Markdown source, a long thread becomes a question-plus-conclusion summary that ends with a pointer to the side-question panel (the full answer stays there). Panel details: the bottom「New question」input hides while a thread follow-up is open (no two similar inputs); the follow-up button reads「Follow up」/「Cancel follow-up」. `Esc` closes the panel unless the settings dialog owns focus; the input is focused when the panel opens; long answers can be expanded and collapsed without losing the reading position. The panel footer has an「Answer only in this panel」toggle (same as `echoAnswer`, no need to open Settings). ## Side effects & risks - **Spends one model call** per side question (a fork of the current conversation). - **Creates a child session**, then archives it. If archiving is unavailable the child stays visible in the session list — the answer itself is unaffected. - **Writes** `/btw/.jsonl` (up to `historyLimit` records per session; default 50, configurable 1–200; atomically replaced). Two side questions in the same session cannot lose each other's record: appends are serialized per file inside the host process. It never copies the main conversation to disk. - **Read-only is enforced in-process by a tool guard**, not by prompt text: the guard is armed on the side-question child's own scope, so a tool call from that child is denied with a model-facing reason while other sessions stay unaffected. The scope mechanics are confirmed against the shipped host source on DSH 0.2.2-rc.5 (`tools.guard()` registers in the calling scope; `checkGuards()` walks `[global, ...agent scope chain]`); an end-to-end live denial was not re-run for this release (**pending live verification**). If the child context cannot be resolved — not observed in practice — no guard is armed, a warning is logged, and read-only falls back to the prompt only. - **Cost warning on very large sessions**: above a 250K-token parent context (the host's context pressure), the panel shows one warning line with the projected 0.75–1.2× range and the last actual side-question prompt size; `/btw` appends the same line to its result. It never blocks the question. - **Optional bounded mode (`boundedContext`)**: above 400K tokens, a side question can run on a `spawn` child that only sees the last 12 user/assistant messages (700 chars each, 4000 total) plus the question. Cost is bounded by the digest plus the host's fixed subagent overhead (tens of thousands of tokens; ~119K on a heavily loaded profile, vs 762K for a full fork on the same session), but older context is dropped and answers are marked `bounded`. Off by default; fork cache reuse is lost in this mode. The parent transcript is read only when the mode triggers (previously every side question materialized it, even with the mode off). If the digest ends up with no messages, the run logs a warning and falls back to a full fork — and that fallback costs the usual fork amount. ## Uninstall & leftovers Removing the plugin removes **code only**; it never deletes data it wrote: - `/btw/.jsonl` — side-question history, one file per parent session; - `/btw/settings.json` — the settings saved from **Settings → Side questions**. `` defaults to `~/.dsh` (configurable with the `dataRoot` plugin config). To clean up completely after uninstalling, delete `/btw/`. Side questions also leave **archived child sessions** in the host's own session store — that data belongs to DSH, not to this plugin, and is managed with the host's session list. ## Compatibility | Plugin | Verified on DSH | | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 0.6.0 | 0.2.2-rc.3 | | 0.6.0 | 0.2.2-rc.5 | | 0.6.1 | 0.2.2-rc.5 | | 0.6.2 | 0.2.2-rc.5（发布后 `--npm` web 复验 + 线上索引 13/13 + live 桌面重启后复验） | | 0.6.3 | 0.2.2-rc.5（发布后 `--npm` web 复验 + 线上索引 13/13 + 临时宿主 bounded e2e + live 桌面重启后手测） | The underlying host seams (command dispatch while busy, fork cache reuse, `tools.guard`, `workspaceRegistry.archiveSession`) were verified on DSH 0.2.2-rc.3 and re-checked unchanged on 0.2.2-rc.5 ([runtime rc.5](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md): a 43-package diff found no change in any seam this plugin uses). End-to-end status: for the published 0.6.0, the web smoke passes **15 PASS / 3 SKIP / 0 FAIL** and the deep smoke (real model calls) passes **30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL**; on DSH 0.2.2-rc.5 both were re-run (15/3/0 and **30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, the deep run leaving a `status=done` history record), plus the live desktop regression **18 PASS / 1 SKIP** (and **22 PASS / 1 SKIP** with `--deep`, which writes a real `~/.dsh/btw` record). The remaining deep SKIP is a data-dependent branch (the thread-card assertion runs before the first submit). The deep smoke warms the session up with one ordinary message first, because a slash command renders no conversation card in a **blank** session ([runtime rc.5 §5.2](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md#52-命令卡片只在非空白会话里渲染2026-11-20-实测)). The desktop regression against the **installed 0.6.0** (real desktop profile, after restart) passes **25 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, and `pnpm gate btw` passes the full 4-step gate. **0.6.1** fixes two 0.6.0 leftovers: promotion no longer blows up the main composer (a long thread used to insert a 1262-character draft that rendered ~62 lines; it is now fitted to at most six lines at the measured composer width, with the full answer left in the panel), and the host half now actually reads its Chinese/English locale files (0.6.0 kept showing the English `FALLBACK` for `/btw` command results because the nested locale table never matched the flat keys). On DSH 0.2.2-rc.5: web **15 PASS / 3 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, web `--deep` **30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, desktop **25 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, desktop `--deep` **23 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL** (the extra assertion is the composer-height threshold). DSH has **no host-side locale service** and passes command text through verbatim ([runtime rc.5 §8.1](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md)), so a plugin must localize itself; and replacing `client.js` in a live desktop may keep serving the previously cached bundle until the app restarts ([runtime rc.5 §8.2](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md)). The **published 0.6.3** was verified from npm: web `--npm` **15 PASS / 3 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, `--npm --deep` **30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, online index **13/13**, and a bounded e2e on a real 668K-token session produced a `mode="bounded"` record with **21,503** total tokens (vs 762,526 for a full fork) and `· bounded` in the command result. The live desktop was restarted and re-checked: the bounded checkbox in settings persists to `settings.json`, and a 668K-token session produced a `mode="bounded"` record with **118,730** total tokens (vs 762,526 for a full fork on the same session) whose result carries `· bounded` and no fork-cost warning ([runtime rc.5 §8.2](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md)). The **published 0.6.2** was verified from npm: web `--npm` **15 PASS / 3 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, `--npm --deep` **30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, online index **13/13** (lists 0.6.2); its panel warning was e2e-checked on a real 668K-token session in a temporary host. The live desktop was restarted and re-checked: the panel warning renders on a real 668K-token session (`[data-btw-cost-hint="warn"]`), and desktop `--deep` passes **30 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL** ([runtime rc.5 §8.2](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md)). The **published 0.6.1** was re-verified from npm: web smoke **15 PASS / 3 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, web `--deep` **30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, desktop regression **23 PASS / 1 SKIP** (blank session), and the online plugin index lists 0.6.1 (index smoke **13/13**). ## License MIT

# @kangyishuai/dsh-casefile

> Evidence-first workbench for REA inside DeepSeek Harness: turn observations into citable evidence, handoff-ready spec packs, and recomputable acceptance — instead of conclusions that die with the session.

[中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

Unofficial plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Not affiliated with DeepSeek. It is an adapter on top of [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) (MIT); it ships none of REA's code and no analysis engine.

> **Status: M3 complete (five checkers + one-call cycle + near-miss + coverage gate + report).** Persists projects, evidence, claims, features, unknowns, obligations and check records; exports a redacted spec pack; ships a workbench page (evidence / obligations / runs), a sidebar entry and a settings section. A **builder session** can be started from a project: casefile creates a child session, feeds it only the spec pack (never the original target), and returns the session id; `awaitBuilder` reports why it stopped. The build/check loop runs real commands: `case_build start` records a `BuildRun` with an implementation digest, `case_check run` records a result bound to that digest, and a later build whose digest differs automatically **reopens** the obligations it had closed. Verified by the package unit suite (counts and commands are listed in [docs/testing/casefile.md](../../docs/testing/casefile.md)) plus a web end-to-end smoke on a throwaway DSH home (including the stale-reopen path) and a desktop read-only regression. Treat it as young software.

## What it does

REA is very good at producing evidence-backed observations. What it does not do is keep them: the evidence lives inside the tool results of one session and is gone when the session ends.

Casefile is the missing layer:

- **Projects as first-class objects.** One target = one project directory under the plugin's data root, with its authorization tier (`owned` / `authorized` / `research`), scope (`all` / `selected`), and recorded REA version and capability hash.
- **Evidence ledger.** Each observation is stored as an `Evidence` record that keeps REA's own `confidence` (observed / derived / inferred) and `authority` (shipped-artifact / controlled-replay / live-observation / external), plus a `limitations` list and optional integrity value. Casefile never re-derives those judgments.
- **Claims you can cite and select.** A `Claim` is the unit you quote in a handoff: it references evidence ids, carries its own limitations, and can be selected (`case_claim select`) for export.
- **Feature grouping for scoped work.** Group selected claims into a `Feature` with boundaries and non-goals — the unit later used by "rebuild only these features".
- **Unknowns are shipped, not hidden.** Open unknowns are part of the spec pack; a pack that silently drops them is a lie.
- **Spec pack export.** `case_brief export` writes `spec/<timestamp>/spec.json` + `brief.md`: selected claims, their evidence, features, open unknowns, a coverage summary, and a content hash. Redaction is on by default and shared by spec packs, machine-readable bundles **and** the HTML/Markdown acceptance report (see [Privacy](#side-effects--risks)).

## Redaction

All three exports (spec pack, bundle, report) go through the same `redactPack` pass, and `case_project report` redacts by default too:

- **Paths:** any path under a common system root (`/Users`, `/home`, `/var`, `/tmp`, `/private`, `/Applications`, `/Volumes`, `/opt`, `/etc`, `/Library`, `/usr`, `/System`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/dev`, `/proc`, `/boot`, `/root`, `/mnt`, `/media`, `/snap`, `/nix`, `/data`, `/srv`, `/workspace`), any unexpanded `~/…`, and any **absolute** path ending in a **1–8 character** file extension — replaced with `<path>`.
- **Tokens:** `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `github_pat_…`, AWS `AKIA…`/`ASIA…`, Google `AIza…`, `npm_…`, `xox[abp]-…`, `Bearer …`, JWT (`eyJ…`), PEM private-key blocks, and `password=` / `api_key=` / `secret=` / `token=` values — replaced with `[redacted]`.
- **Deliberately kept:** URLs and API routes **without a file extension** (`https://example.test/api/todos`, `POST /api/todos`, `/auth/token`) stay readable, because a spec pack that turns every route into `<path>` is useless to the builder. An absolute path ending in a file extension is redacted even when it looks like a route (`/static/app.js`, `/api/v1/openapi.json`).

Known limit: a path that contains spaces is redacted only up to the first space (the remainder stays). Redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee: review a pack before sharing it.
- **Capability detection.** `case_project` and `diagnose()` report whether `mcp__rea__*` tools are visible and which casefile-required tools are missing, instead of silently degrading.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kangyishuai/dsh-casefile
```

To run the working tree instead of a published version, pack it first — `link:` installs do not work (the host's `@deepseek-ai/*` resolution only covers packages whose real path is inside the profile):

```bash
cd packages/casefile
pnpm pack --pack-destination /tmp
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /tmp/kangyishuai-dsh-casefile-*.tgz
```

Re-run `pnpm pack` + `add` after changing the code. Restart the DSH desktop app afterwards (this plugin is a host half).

## Requirements

- A REA MCP server registered in DSH, exposing tools named `mcp__rea__*` (REA's own `rea setup`, or any community bridge). Casefile **does not** register that row itself — it would collide with REA's `rea-mcp` entry.
- Casefile works without REA for manual evidence entry, but capability detection will report `missing` and later milestones' checks will degrade.

## Workbench

The plugin adds a **Casefile** entry to the sidebar. The page lists projects on the left and shows the selected project on the right with three tabs:

- **Evidence** — claims (with confidence, limits and evidence count) and the evidence records they cite;
- **Obligations** — obligations, their status, and open unknowns. Closing an obligation needs a _fresh PASS check bound to the current implementation digest_; otherwise the button names the exact blocker (`no-fresh-check`, `coverage-below`, `open-unknowns`, …) instead of pretending.
- **Runs** — build rounds (status, implementation digest, command) and check verdicts bound to each digest.

The list view opens with an **overview strip** (project count, breakdown by target kind and state, obligation pass/total, unresolved unknowns across projects); `case_project overview` returns the same data as JSON. An **empty** workbench explains in plain words what a case file is, who it is for and what the first step is; tool names (`case_evidence`, `case_claim`, …) are folded under “For developers / the AI agent” instead of being the first thing a new user reads. The **New project** form labels every field (title, target, target kind, authorization) and validates the required title on blur and on submit, with a readable error instead of a dead button.

The panel header shows the selected project's **autonomy level** (L0–L3); the badge's tooltip explains in plain words what the level means, with L0–L3 kept as a subtitle.

The header also exposes a **Trash** entry. It lists projects dropped with `case_project drop` (id, size, file count), restores one with a click, and empties the trash only after a dry-run shows the impact (`N entries / size; unknown entries are kept`). Dropped projects are moved, never deleted, until you confirm the hard delete.

A project's detail page carries a collapsed **Danger zone → Move to trash** entry for the user: it first previews the impact (file count / size, restorable) and only moves the project after an explicit confirmation, then shows it in the trash. The agent-side `case_project drop` tool requires `confirm: true` **and** is documented as "only after the user explicitly agreed, never on your own initiative" — under a full-access permission preset the model could technically call it, so the tool description and this README both put the consent requirement in writing.

Per [ADR 0002](https://github.com/kangyishuai/dsh-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-destructive-operations.md) there is also `case_project purge` (`dryRun` + `confirm`) for scripted use, and every drop/restore/purge is written to the data root's `audit.jsonl` (a dropped project can no longer write into its own audit file).

A settings section shows the data root, project count and REA connection state. REA being absent is shown as an **optional, unavailable notice** (it does not block creating projects or recording evidence), not as an error; the raw `mcp__rea__*` detection detail is available under the same advanced fold.

## Tools

| Tool              | Actions                                     | Purpose                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `case_project`    | `open`, `list`, `get`, `update`             | Open a new **or existing** project, list, inspect, change authorization tier / scope / state                     |
| `case_evidence`   | `add`, `list`, `show`                       | Store an REA observation as evidence; filter; read one                                                           |
| `case_claim`      | `add`, `list`, `search`, `select`           | Store a citable conclusion; search; select it for export                                                         |
| `case_feature`    | `add`, `list`                               | Group claims into a feature with boundaries and non-goals                                                        |
| `case_unknown`    | `add`, `list`, `resolve`                    | Record unknowns; mark one resolved with a note                                                                   |
| `case_obligation` | `add`, `list`, `close`, `reopen`            | Acceptance obligations; `close` needs a fresh passing check                                                      |
| `case_build`      | `start`, `agent`, `status`, `loop`, `cycle` | Build runs, builder sessions, and the build→check→close loop                                                     |
| `case_check`      | `run`, `list`, `loop`                       | Run one checker and bind the result to the current implementation digest                                         |
| `case_access`     | `await-login`                               | Poll a CDP page until a sign-in predicate holds (ready / timeout / error)                                        |
| `case_app`        | `inspect`                                   | One-screen macOS `.app` summary (bundle id, versions, sandbox, ATS, UTI domains)                                 |
| `case_brief`      | `export`                                    | Write the redacted spec pack (`spec.json` + `brief.md`)                                                          |
| `case_ingest`     | `ingest`, `schema`                          | Ingest an external agent's report under a stable contract (recorded, not endorsed); `schema` prints the contract |

`case_project` also carries `close`, `report` (`format: md | html | both`, redacted by default), `bundle` (machine-readable, deterministic), `overview`, `archive`, `drop` (`dryRun` / `confirm`), `trash`, `restore`, `purge` (`dryRun` / `confirm`), and `autonomy` (L0–L3 gating).

**Session memory:** every call that receives an explicit `projectId` also makes it the session's current project, and that pointer is persisted under the data root — `case_project open` with an existing project id opens it instead of failing, and after a restart the same session can keep calling tools without repeating `projectId`. If a call still omits it, the error names the last opened project as a hint instead of just failing.

Every tool returns `{ ok, data?, error?{code,message,hint}, summary }`; errors carry a stable code, so the model can correct itself instead of guessing.

**Tool-surface cost:** these 12 definitions total ~13.6 KB of `description`+`parameters` JSON (≈3.4K tokens at ~4 bytes/token) and are resident in every session, while only a small fraction of sessions use casefile. That is a deliberate trade-off (each tool keeps a self-explanatory schema); the low-frequency ones (`case_access`, `case_app`, `case_ingest`) are the first candidates to merge into a `case_misc` tool if the surface needs shrinking.

Obligations may carry `featureIds`, so a **scoped replica** can report coverage per feature: an obligation tagged with a feature only counts toward that feature's ratio; untagged ones count only globally.

## Checkers

| Checker | What it judges                                                                 | Verdicts                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `build` | a shell build command: exit code + configured output paths                     | pass / fail / unknown(timeout)                |
| `cli`   | a command against `{ exitCode, stdoutIncludes, stdoutEquals, stderrIncludes }` | pass / fail / unknown(timeout)                |
| `web`   | two PNG screenshots: similarity = 1 − mean-abs-diff/255, plus a size check     | pass / fail / unknown(missing or invalid PNG) |

Screenshots are captured elsewhere (REA's browser tools or any tool the user prefers); the `web` checker only judges. The PNG decoder is in-repo (`lib/core/png.js`, no third-party dependency) and supports 8-bit RGB/RGBA, non-interlaced.

## Authorization tiers

A project carries `authTier`: `owned`, `authorized`, or `research`. Starting a **replica build** (`case_build agent` / `cycle`) is refused when the tier is `research` unless the caller passes `allowResearchTier: true` with a `reason` — the override is written to the project audit log as `auth/research-override`. This keeps the tier from being decorative: a research-only project can be investigated and specified, but not quietly reconstructed.

## Closing a project

`case_project close` refuses until the project is actually done. The gate checks, in order: at least one obligation; no `open`/`fail`/`blocked` obligations; coverage ≥ `minCoverage` (default 100%); no unresolved unknowns; a fresh check whose implementation digest matches the current build. Each blocker is reported by name, so you know what to fix.

`case_project report` writes `reports/<timestamp>/report.md` + `report.json`: coverage (global and per feature), obligation table, check table with implementation digests, unknowns, loop state, and a declaration that `unknown` never means pass.

## Acquisition: ingest, don't acquire

casefile never fetches content itself. Evidence carries a **`producer`** record — tool, version, access mode (`headful` / `headless` / `api` / `archive` / `manual` / `stealth` / `unknown`), output kind, and whether you explicitly confirmed the access method. Reports render a producer table plus one statement: the operator chose and executed the acquisition.

That is what lets you feed it anything: REA's captures, a HAR from your proxy, an HTML snapshot from Scrapling, or a screenshot you took by hand. Tier 1 (human-equivalent browsing, official APIs, public archives) is supported as-is; Tier 2 (your own session, or a mode you label `stealth`) is recorded but not endorsed; Tier 3 (CAPTCHA solving, fingerprint forgery, proxy rotation, bulk high-rate scraping) is not provided and will not be — see [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md#acquisition-boundary-three-tiers--采集边界三段式).

## Clean-room attestation

Every builder session writes an **attestation** (`attestations.jsonl`): the prompt digest, the spec digest, how many claims/evidence items were fed, the auth tier and any research override, and whether the "do not read the original target" clause was actually in the prompt. The report renders it as a `## 净室 attestation` section.

The attestation is deliberately honest about its limits: DSH has no per-agent tool whitelist (see `docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.3.md` §12.7), so isolation is **information-flow only**. The statement says so instead of claiming clean-room certification.

## Anti-false-green

The suite includes **near-miss injection** tests: an obligation is closed against a correct implementation, then one character of the output is changed, and the next round must fail that obligation and reopen it. A failed build also skips checks entirely instead of producing a misleading pass. See `packages/casefile/test/near-miss.test.js`.

## Data layout

Everything lives under the plugin's data root (default `<DSH_HOME>/casefile`, override with `dataRoot`):

```
casefile/
└── projects/<project-id>/
    ├── project.json          # version + target + authTier + scope + REA version
    ├── evidence.jsonl        # append-only; same id later wins
    ├── claims.jsonl
    ├── features.jsonl
    ├── unknowns.jsonl
    ├── audit.jsonl           # who did what, append-only
    └── spec/<timestamp>/     # exported spec.json + brief.md
```

Rules: JSON files carry a `version`; a file written by a newer casefile is reported as read-only instead of silently rewritten. Corrupt JSON is renamed `.broken` and kept. Records are append-only, so a project directory can be reviewed and diffed.

## Config

| Key                | Default               | Meaning                                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dataRoot`         | `<DSH_HOME>/casefile` | Where project data lives; injectable for tests                        |
| `defaultAuthTier`  | `research`            | Default authorization tier for new projects                           |
| `cleanRoomDefault` | `true`                | Reserved for the builder milestone: builder cannot see the original   |
| `checkers`         | `["cli","web"]`       | Reserved for the verification milestone                               |
| `maxRounds`        | `5`                   | Reserved for the verification loop                                    |
| `maxArtifactBytes` | `67108864` (64 MiB)   | Reject archiving artifacts larger than this (stat pre-check, no read) |

Config is read from the `casefile` row in `cordis.patch.yml`. Do not edit the profile by hand — change the row's `config:`.

## Compatibility

| Plugin          | Verified on DSH                   | What was run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0.1.x–0.2.x     | 0.2.2-rc.3 (macOS, desktop + web) | 138 → 177 unit tests; 52-assertion web end-to-end smoke on a throwaway DSH home; **14-assertion desktop read-only regression on a real Electron renderer (CDP)**; `pnpm gate casefile` 4/4 steps green.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 0.3.x–0.5.x     | same                              | 172 → 177 unit tests; adds `case_access` (sign-in wait), `case_app` (app-bundle first hop), artifact archiving, and project `archive`/`drop`; **exercised on 8 real projects** (local macOS app, sign-in-gated page, external-collector ingestion).                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **0.6.x–0.8.x** | same                              | 216 unit tests; **56-assertion web end-to-end** (adds external-report ingest dryRun/real assertions); **15-assertion desktop regression** (adds autonomy badge); `pnpm gate casefile` 4/4 green. Adds: HTML report, machine-readable bundle, L3 unattended runs, external-report ingest contract (incl. automatic Craft-shaped mapping), blank-screenshot guard.                                                                      |
| 0.8.1           | 0.2.2-rc.5 (macOS, desktop + web) | No code change needed for this DSH build. 216 unit tests; **56-assertion web end-to-end smoke**; **15-assertion desktop read-only regression (run twice, idempotent)**; `pnpm gate casefile` 4/4 steps green, plus **`pnpm gate:all --repeat 2`** green across all six plugins (631s). The 43-package host diff for this release ([runtime rc.5](../../docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.5.md)) found no change in any host API this plugin uses. |

Host APIs used here were verified by runtime inspection; the findings are recorded in `docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.3.md` §10 (including two pitfalls: a missed `declareRemote` silently 404s only that endpoint, and `agentPresets` cannot be composed from bundle names).

**Five** target kinds were exercised in real tasks (incl. a local Electron app): **a local macOS app bundle** (Info.plist, signature surface, binary inventory — the binary layer needs REA + Ghidra, see `docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.3.md` §13–§14), **a sign-in-gated web page** (`case_access await-login`, structure-only capture), **external-collector artifacts** (`producer` + `artifactPath` archiving), and **an app's own release package** (survey → spec → acceptance, closed end to end).

## Side effects & risks

- **Files it writes:** only under the data root above. It never writes into the investigated project, never modifies the REA binary, and never edits the profile.
- **Destructive actions:** following [ADR 0002](https://github.com/kangyishuai/dsh-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-destructive-operations.md). `case_project drop` moves the whole project directory into `<dataRoot>/trash/<timestamp>-<id>` (recoverable), needs `confirm: true`, supports `dryRun` with a count / size / target path, and writes a data-root audit entry. The tool contract says the agent must only call it **after the user explicitly agreed**; the workbench offers the same action to the user behind a preview + confirmation (Danger zone). Note that under a `danger-full-access` / `approval: never` preset the host does not add an approval prompt for this tool — full-access sessions are trusted to follow their instructions, so this consent requirement is documented rather than enforced by the host. The trash can be listed, restored and emptied (`case_project purge`, `dryRun` + `confirm`; unknown entries in the trash are kept and reported, never `rm -rf`ed). Nothing is hard-deleted without an explicit confirmation.
- **Privacy:** project data stays on this machine. Spec packs, bundles and reports are redacted by default (system-root paths, `~/…`, extended paths, and the token shapes listed above) but **you should still review a file before sharing it** — redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee.
- **Evidence quality:** casefile stores what you tell it. It does not verify an observation, and it never upgrades a claim's confidence or authority.
- **Legal:** intended for research and for software you own or are authorized to analyze. It deliberately ships **no** DRM/anti-debugging bypass and no way to reuse third-party assets. Read [DISCLAIMER.md](./DISCLAIMER.md) before use.

## Uninstall

Uninstalling the plugin does **not** delete anything: the host only removes the package. Your case files stay on disk under the data root (`<DSH_HOME>/casefile` by default — see [Data layout](#data-layout)):

- `projects/<id>/` — project records plus `artifacts/`, `spec/`, `reports/`, `bundles/` and `checks/`;
- `trash/` — projects moved there by `case_project drop` (still restorable if you reinstall);
- `audit.jsonl`, `last-opened.json`, `session-pointers.json` — the data-root audit trail and session pointers.

Nothing is uploaded, and nothing is cleaned up on uninstall — deliberately, so a reinstall keeps your evidence. To delete the data manually (only after you have exported what you need):

```bash
du -sh "$DSH_HOME/casefile"   # see the size first
rm -rf "$DSH_HOME/casefile"   # use your configured dataRoot if you overrode it
```

Exported spec packs, reports and bundles live **inside** the project directories (`spec/`, `reports/`, `bundles/`), so they are removed with the tree; copy them out first if they matter.

## Development

```bash
pnpm verify        # lint + typecheck + plugin checks + tests
pnpm check         # plugin conventions + index metadata
pnpm test          # package unit tests
```
