# @kangyishuai/dsh-next-step

> A next-step decision card for DeepSeek Harness: after a completed answer that looks worth continuing, a compact card shows where the conversation stands, the question you need to settle, and 1–2 mutually exclusive proposals. Click one and that pill's text — exactly as written on it — is sent as your user message. **How often cards appear is a switch you own** (strict / balanced / eager); when one is withheld, a one-click button reveals the candidate the plugin already computed, with no second model call. It also keeps a **local review log** so the thresholds, the wording and the buttons can be tuned against evidence instead of vibes. Optionally — off by default — a grey ghost hint in the empty composer offers the next prompt, accepted with `Tab` or `→`.

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@kangyishuai/dsh-next-step?color=cb3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kangyishuai/dsh-next-step) [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/verified%20on%20DSH-0.2.2--rc.5-4b6bfb)](#compatibility) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)

[中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

Unofficial plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Not affiliated with DeepSeek.

> **Status: early.** Verified against the current target DSH version — see the [Compatibility](#compatibility) table. Both faces sit on host seams that are not public API, so a DSH upgrade can silently disable them (read [Side effects & risks](#side-effects--risks) first). Young software: keep your own notes of anything you would hate to lose.

![Decision card under a completed answer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kangyishuai/dsh-plugins/main/packages/next-step/docs/images/decision-card.png)

## What it does

- **A card when there is something to continue — as often as _you_ want.** When a turn ends normally, the plugin makes one extra model call that asks the model to grade the turn on a three-level scale (`must` / `could` / `no`, with "when in doubt say `could`" written into the prompt). A setting decides which levels are shown: **Strict** (`must` only), **Balanced** (default: `must` + `could`) or **Eager** (everything, including `no` — an experimental calibration mode). The card itself is always computed; the tier only decides whether it is displayed. When it is shown, a decision card is appended below the answer: a one-to-three sentence **summary** of the conversation state (folded to two lines, with an expand/collapse control when it is longer), one **question** that names the decision you have to make, and **1–2 pills** for mutually exclusive directions (one is fine when the next step is obvious — no padding). Each pill carries the exact sentence that will be sent when you click it: **2–20 characters, verb-first, and it must name a concrete object from the conversation** (file, command, flag, version, PR number). Generic pills like “check whether the definition is accurate” are dropped — if none survive, no card is shown at all.
- **One click is one user message.** Clicking a pill puts that pill's own text into the composer and submits it through the same path as pressing Enter yourself — not by faking a session event. An idle session sends immediately; if a turn is already running, the text is queued exactly like a typed message.
- **It stays.** Cards and decisions are appended to the session log as plugin records and folded by a session projection, which is the only source of truth. A page reload, a session switch or an app restart brings them back; the client keeps no separate state.
- **Resolved, not removed — and not noise.** After you click, the card stays in the transcript but becomes read-only: summary and question remain, the pills are replaced by the one you picked in a selected state (✓ plus its text), followed by a grey “sent” line. **Cards from earlier turns that were never decided default to a single folded line** (“Earlier turn · first sentence of the summary”); the full summary stays in the hover title and in the session log. In the real usage data 82% of shown cards were never decided, so leaving every old card expanded meant the only way to stop the noise was to turn the feature off (audit AUD-NS-02). At most one card is interactive at a time. The ✕ in a card's corner dismisses it without sending anything.
- **Ghost hint in the composer (off by default).** The same model call also produces one next prompt. With the ghost face enabled, an empty idle composer shows it as grey, placeholder-style text. `Tab` or `→` accepts it into the draft (undoable with `Ctrl+Z`), `Esc` clears the current suggestion, typing makes it disappear, and it stays hidden while the composer holds a draft, an attachment, an `@` reference or a slash command. The ghost is not draft content, so pressing Enter on an otherwise empty composer sends nothing.
- **Two faces, one call.** Card and ghost are produced together by a single model call — turning the ghost on costs no additional requests.
- **Withheld cards are one click away, and free.** A turn whose card the tier withheld still gets the small “Generate a next-step card” button under the answer. Clicking it **reveals the candidate that was already computed** — no second model call, no 20-second wait. Only a turn that never produced a candidate (the call failed or timed out) actually calls the model again. Clicking that button is also the strongest evidence that the tier withheld something you wanted.
- **A local review log, so tuning has evidence.** Every eligible turn appends one line to `<dataRoot>/next-step/events.jsonl`: which gate decided, the three-level grade, latency, token usage, what you did with the card afterwards (clicked / dismissed / ignored / typed your own message / revealed it / **walked away — no message for 15 minutes, recorded as `typed:false`**), and whether the card ever entered the viewport. Nothing is uploaded, and your message text is never written — only lengths, delays and how many concrete objects overlapped with a pill. **One exception: the pill labels the model generated are recorded verbatim** (the review has to look at the button wording; they are concrete objects lifted from the conversation, not your prose). From the settings section you can generate a Markdown report (kept: the latest 20) whose verdict sentences only appear once there are enough data points (80 turns / 25 cards).
- **Switches that actually stop requests.** `card` (default on) and `ghost` (default off) are separate switches; the global `enabled` switch off means no generation request at all, not just a hidden UI. A pause and a per-session card budget (`maxCardsPerSession`) stop new cards too. Cards already in the log stay readable.

## Cost & model calls

- One extra model call per trigger, on the model the session's agent is currently using (falling back to the default model selection), billed to your own provider quota.
- The call times out after 20 s. Other failures, rate limits and malformed JSON are silent: no card, no dialog — only a counter in the plugin's diagnostics. **One recovery attempt is allowed, and it always carries the same conversation**: if the model returns an _empty_ answer the request is simply resent (an empty string is not a formatting problem — asking the model to "repair" nothing is how content-free cards used to get written); if it returns something malformed but non-empty, the repair request repeats the transcript and asks only for the format. A card that cannot point at anything in the conversation is dropped and counted as `ungrounded`. A **timeout or cancellation** is counted separately (the `aborted` counter plus a "Last skipped" reason such as `generation timeout after 20s`), and the generate button then says the generation timed out or was cancelled — so this class stays diagnosable afterwards. **Sending your next message no longer aborts an in-flight generation**: that call runs to completion and is stored as a hidden candidate (`shown:false`), so no stale card is pushed into the transcript; it shows up as `superseded` in “Last skipped” and in the report's gate distribution (audit AUD-NS-01). **Be clear about what this buys:** it does **not** save tokens — aborting billed only what had already streamed, while running to completion bills the full output, so these calls now cost **more**; the gain is that a nearly-finished call is no longer thrown away and that cancellations become explainable in diagnostics and review. Such candidates do **not** count against `maxCardsPerSession`, never report an impression, and **cannot be revealed** (the generate button only works for the latest normally completed turn). Malformed output is dropped without writing a record.
- When the model grades the turn `no` (or `could`, and your tier is Strict), the candidate is stored but not shown — **the call still happens**: the tier saves UI noise, not tokens. Revealing a withheld candidate later costs nothing (no second call).
- The review log is a local append-only file that rotates at 2 MB (`events.jsonl` + one `.1` history). It contains no message text, but it does record the generated pill labels verbatim (the review needs the button wording); it is on by default and can be switched off in the settings ("Local usage data").
- No other network access, no telemetry.

## Side effects & risks

- **Appends plugin records to the session log.** One card record per generated card, one decision record per click or dismissal. Nothing is edited or deleted; uninstalling stops rendering them, but the records stay in the log.
- **Spends model quota** on every completed turn while the card face is on — see [Cost & model calls](#cost--model-calls).
- **A click overwrites the composer draft.** Sending the pill text goes through the composer shell (`setDraft`, then `submit`), which replaces whatever was in the draft. To protect you, both pills are **disabled while the composer holds any draft**, and the hover hint asks you to clear it first.
- **What is sent is a normal user message.** It enters the model context and is visible in the transcript exactly as if you had typed it.
- **Private host seams.** The card renders through `conversation.chat.turnTail`; state comes from a host session projection read via `useProjection`; click-to-send uses the composer shell (`setDraft` / `submit`, waiting for the draft to settle before submitting); the ghost uses `conversation.input.overlay` and the host's placeholder DOM. These are internal, untyped and unversioned: a DSH upgrade can make the card, the send path or the ghost stop working **silently**. The plugin degrades instead of breaking a session, but after an upgrade run `pnpm probe:runtime` and the smoke suites, and check diagnostics.
- **The ghost is coupled to the host placeholder DOM**, which is why it ships off by default; if that DOM changes, the hint can simply disappear.
- **Silent failure is by design.** “No card appeared” is not an error dialog; look at the diagnostics counters before filing a bug. Timeouts and cancellations are the one exception worth knowing: they are labelled rather than lumped into a generic failure, because an unlabelled abort is what made one “no card” incident undiagnosable.
- **Writes two things under the data root.** (a) The existing session log gets one card record per generated card — including withheld candidates, so `shown` grows by at most one small record per eligible turn; (b) `<dataRoot>/next-step/events.jsonl` (review log, 2 MB rotation) plus `report-*.md` when you ask for one (the newest 20 are kept, older ones are deleted inside that plugin directory only). **No message text is ever written to the log** (pill labels are recorded verbatim — see above), and nothing leaves the machine.
- **Subagent sessions never get cards**, and only normally completed turns are eligible.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kangyishuai/dsh-next-step
```

To run the working tree instead of a published version, pack it first — `link:` installs do not work (the host's `@deepseek-ai/*` resolution only covers packages whose real path is inside the profile):

```bash
cd packages/next-step
pnpm pack --pack-destination /tmp
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /tmp/kangyishuai-dsh-next-step-*.tgz
```

Re-run `pnpm pack` + `add` after changing the code. The plugin has a host half, so restart the DSH desktop app and refresh the page.

## Usage

**The card.** It appears under the last answer once that turn has completed, and it never steals focus. Each pill carries the exact sentence it will send; click it to send that sentence. If the summary is folded, use the small expand button to read it all. ✕ dismisses the card; earlier cards default to a single folded line (“Earlier turn · first sentence of the summary”) with the full summary on hover.

**Keyboard.** While the card is interactive, the composer is empty and the session is idle, `⌘↵` / `Ctrl+↵` sends the primary pill (same path as a click). When the composer holds a draft, an attachment, an open `@`/`/` menu, or a turn is running, the combination keeps its host Queue/Steer meaning — the plugin does not steal it.

**When no card appears.** A turn can end up without a visible card for two different reasons: the model graded it `no` (or `could` while your tier is Strict), in which case the card **already exists but is withheld**; or generation was skipped/failed (paused, messages queued, budget, timeout, bad output), in which case there is no candidate at all. In both cases a small “Generate a next-step card” button appears under the latest answer. For a withheld card, clicking it **reveals the stored candidate — instantly, with no second model call**; only when there is no candidate does it actually call the model again. So when you think a card should have appeared: check “Last skipped” in the settings diagnostics, and click that button.

**The ghost hint.** Turn the ghost face on in the plugin settings. With an empty, idle composer you see the latest card's next prompt in grey, aligned with the host placeholder. `Tab` or `→` accepts it — the text lands in the draft and stays undoable. `Esc` clears it for this suggestion, and the first typed character hides it. It only ever edits the draft: it does not send, and it does not bind Enter.

**Where the switches are.** The plugin's settings expose the two faces (`card` / `ghost`), the global switch, the pause and the per-session budget. The global switch off stops requests entirely, not just rendering.

## Settings & diagnostics

Settings → **Next-step suggestions** (its own section now, no longer a row buried in General) has everything you need to control it:

The section opens with **three rows** — enable, **card frequency** (strict / balanced / eager, changeable in place) and the card switch — and everything else sits under a **“More settings”** disclosure (collapsed by default):

- **Local usage data** — the review log switch (default on).
- **Ghost hint in the composer** — the second face's switch (default off).
- **Cadence** — “Pause for 1 hour” / “Resume”.
- **Per session, at most N cards** — the budget (`maxCardsPerSession`, clamped to 0–1000, default **60**). It only counts cards that were _shown_; withheld candidates do not consume it. The default dropped from 120 to 60 because real usage peaked at 80 cards in a session and the 120 limit was never hit (the budget gate never fired); an existing settings file whose value is **exactly 120** follows the new default on upgrade, while any other value you chose is left alone.
- **Review** — the four numbers that matter (card rate / click-through / ignore rate / misses), a one-line verdict when the sample is big enough, and a **“Generate report”** button that writes `report-YYYYMMDD-HHmmss.md` next to the log.
- **Diagnostics** — generated (with how many were withheld) / failed / aborted / skipped / in-flight counters, the **reason the last card was skipped** (model judged unnecessary / queued / paused / budget / failure / timeout / cancelled / you already started the next turn, with the model's own sentence), the last error, the runtime **version + build hash**, and a Refresh button. `nextStep/diagnostics` returns the same `version` / `buildHash` / `buildFiles` / `packagePath`, so a running build can be matched against `dsh plugin list` or the npm tarball without digging through startup logs. Caveat: `buildHash` covers `package.json`, and pnpm rewrites it during a `file:` install — in that case compare against the installed copy, not the repo (see [docs/testing §4.5](../../docs/testing/next-step.md)).

Turning the global switch off **hides every dependent row** (card / ghost / pause / budget / diagnostics) and leaves just the switch plus one line of explanation — off means off, nothing looks like it still runs, and re-enabling restores the previous switch values.

The row writes the same `$DSH_HOME/next-step.settings.json` that the host re-reads (1 s cache) before every generation, so a change applies on the next turn — no restart. If the row is missing because a host seam moved, editing the file still works.

## When no card appears

| Situation                                                                                         | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The turn was stopped, errored, or produced no text                                                | No card: only normally completed turns are eligible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Subagent session                                                                                  | No card, by design.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Global switch off                                                                                 | No request is made at all; existing cards remain in the transcript.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Paused, or the session's card budget (`maxCardsPerSession`) used up                               | No new card; existing cards stay.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A card or a decision already exists for that turn                                                 | One card per turn; no duplicates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| The model grades the turn `no`, or grades it `could` while your tier is Strict (`shown: false`)   | The candidate is stored but hidden; the generate button **reveals it for free**. “Last skipped” shows the model's reason.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Model call failed, was rate-limited, bad JSON, or the card did not refer to this conversation     | Silent; only a diagnostics counter goes up (`schema` / `ungrounded`). The generate button says the card was dropped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| No conversation content to work from (host seam moved / empty session)                            | No request at all: `no-context` in “Last skipped”. A card from nothing would be a card about nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| The generation **timed out (20 s) or was cancelled**                                              | Counted in `aborted`; “Last skipped” says which, and the generate button reports it. No dialog.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| The generation was still running when you sent your next message (a new turn started)             | **No longer cancelled**: the call finishes and is stored as a `shown:false` candidate (**not a saving** — finishing bills more output tokens than aborting did; the candidate never enters the transcript, never counts against the budget, never reports an impression and cannot be revealed); “Last skipped” shows `superseded`. If you press generate while such a stale call is still running, that call is cancelled first, so the button generates for the latest turn instead of returning `inflight`. |
| The reply is still streaming                                                                      | Nothing is rendered for the turn until it ends.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| The composer already has a draft                                                                  | The card is visible but the pills are disabled until the draft is cleared.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Ghost face on, but the composer is not plain (draft, attachment, `@`, `/`, or a non-idle session) | The hint stays hidden.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Known limitations

- **The card sits under the answer** (`conversation.chat.turnTail`), not in the composer area. It is right below the last answer after the turn completes, so it needs no scrolling; cards from earlier turns scroll with the transcript (see ADR 0009 §4).
- **No card while messages are queued.** If you already have 2+ messages waiting to be sent, the plugin skips generation for that turn (the official action cards use the same limit); nothing is queued or sent by the plugin itself.
- **One or two proposals.** Options must point in different (mutually exclusive) directions; a one-option card means the next step is obvious, not that the card is incomplete.
- **`⌘↵` / `Ctrl+↵` is only taken over when the composer is clean, the session is idle and a card is interactive.** Otherwise the combination keeps its host Queue/Steer complementary-send meaning; the plugin never steals it.
- **“Walked away” is recorded up to 15 minutes late.** The host has no “session switched away” event, so when a card was neither clicked nor dismissed and you never typed, the negative feedback is settled by a TTL (15 minutes) as `typed:false`; if you quit the app before that, the record is never written. At most 32 sessions are tracked at once — the oldest is settled first instead of growing without bound.
- **Superseded candidates are not shown in the UI, and they do not save tokens.** A candidate that finished after the next turn had already started is stored with `shown:false`, never rendered, never fed to the ghost hint, never counted against `maxCardsPerSession`, never reported as an impression, and not revealable from the generate button (that button only works for the latest normally completed turn). Its purpose is to keep a nearly-finished call from being thrown away and to make this case explainable in review — the cost is that those calls **run to completion and bill more output tokens**, so this is not a token-saving change, and it does not backfill cards for old turns.
- **No cross-device sync.** Cards and decisions live in the local session log of the machine that generated them.
- **No cards in subagent sessions**, and none for interrupted or empty turns.
- **The ghost only offers the latest card's next prompt**, and only when the composer is empty and idle.
- **A card must be anchored in the conversation.** Besides the shape checks, the plugin mechanically verifies that the card is _about_ the material the model was given — either it names a concrete object that appears verbatim (file, command, version, PR number, identifier), or it shares at least two four-character Chinese phrases with it (so a paraphrasing card on a one-sentence answer still counts). Otherwise the card is discarded. Known gap: text that only ever appeared inside a tool result is not counted, because the check reads user/assistant text. See [ADR 0023](../../docs/adr/0023-next-step-grounded-cards.md).
- **The card text is model output.** The plugin validates the shape (1–2 options, distinct stances, a 2–20 character label that names a concrete object from the conversation) and drops only the individual options that fail; it never rewrites the wording.
- **A click sends exactly the pill's text** — there is no hidden “short label, long instruction behind it” layer. A `text` field left over in card records written by older versions is ignored.

![After a click: the summary and question stay, the pills disappear](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kangyishuai/dsh-plugins/main/packages/next-step/docs/images/after-click.png)

# @kangyishuai/dsh-projects

> Project-level context for DeepSeek Harness: group sessions into projects, inject project instructions and memory, run isolated parallel threads, and coordinate them with an optional auditable coordinator.

[中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

Unofficial plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Not affiliated with DeepSeek.

> **Note on coordinator context (2026-11-17, DSH 0.2.2-rc.3):** the host's per-session runtime context is not
> delivered to the coordinator session, so project rules, the memory index **and the persona travel inside the
> wake envelope** instead — one letter per turn, carrying the thread's result too.
> Details: `docs/runtime/0.2.2-rc.3.md` §11.24–§11.26.

> **Status: M2–M6 shipped (0.10.x, pre-1.0).** Projects, context injection, isolated parallel threads, an opt-in
> coordinator, the gated approval/executor layer and the Claude-Projects UI alignment (plus its review rounds) are
> implemented and covered by **710 unit tests**, a **270-assertion web end-to-end smoke**, and a **desktop read-only
> regression (17–20 assertions, data-dependent)** that has been run against a live desktop. Remote writes
> (push / PR / merge) are verified **on real GitHub** as well as locally (bare remote + stub `gh`). See the
> compatibility table below for per-version numbers. Project **sharing** is deferred ([ADR 0018](../../docs/adr/0018-projects-defer-liveshare-sharing.md)).

## What it does

DSH groups sessions by working directory and gives the model no project-level memory. This plugin adds the missing layer:

- **Project as a first-class context unit** — a durable record with a goal, directories, budget, and policy. Session membership is stored by the plugin (not derived from an immutable `cwd`).
- **Project instructions and memory injection** — every session attached to a project receives the project's standing rules and `MEMORY.md` index before each request (registered once, rendered per session; sessions belonging to no project get nothing).
- **Project-level budget gate** — a daily thread cap and a concurrent cap are enforced before a thread is created (token-level spend caps come with the coordinator).
- **Pause, archive, delete** — pause is reversible and blocks new threads **and pauses the project's host schedules** (routines and `schedule` reminders stop being delivered, so a pause really stops token spend); archive and delete reconcile the same host entries, and a delete is refused while any of them cannot be removed. Delete follows ADR 0002: one-line impact (threads, size, running, restorable), a two-step confirm, and everything moved into `trash/` with a `manifest.json`.
- **In-app notifications** — a global overlay poller raises a toast when a thread newly fails or starts waiting on you; the browser Notification API stays off by default.
- **Local advantages, settings and memory (B3)** — memory is now an index plus separate fragment files (`memory/fragments/<slug>.md`, listed with preview and a per-entry "forget"; plain `MEMORY.md` entries can be forgotten individually by a stable content id). Project instructions keep the 16,000-char budget and are de-duplicated against what the host's `dsh-agent-instructions` already injected (duplicate paragraphs are dropped and the injection says how many), the whole block is wrapped in `<project-context>` and explicitly labelled "this is project memory, not AGENTS.md". `goal` is capped at 8,000 chars with a counter. New projects ship a conservative default budget (20 threads/day, 2 concurrent, 60 steps, tokens unlimited) editable in settings. **Pause now only stops new threads and schedules — it no longer silently stops context injection.** Settings has four sections (General / Memory / Usage / Debug access); Usage reports tokens and context usage only and **never money** (the host has no price API); notifications have per-project switches (failed and waiting on, completed off). A read-only `gh auth status` / `gh repo list` check reports "not installed / not logged in / missing repo scope" with the exact command to run. The project template writes an idempotent managed block into `AGENTS.md` (user content outside the block is never touched). Thread rename and `@` mention candidates (projects + threads) are exposed as RPCs; the `@` source is registered through `ctx.inject(["inputTriggers"])` and only reports `registered` after `registerSource()` returns successfully (the panel says `unavailable` when the service is missing instead of pretending). The three-key folder card is an **execution gate**, not a note: `Deny` blocks the approval executor's in-folder `gh`/`git` commands, `Allow once` is consumed on first use (second run is refused), `Set as default` stays valid, and an untouched folder keeps the old behaviour. Thread rows open the host `contextMenus` on right-click / Shift+F10 (the hand-drawn `⋯` popover remains as the fallback); EN and ZH dictionaries are in sync (106 B3 keys added to both).
- **Library and artifact cards (B5)** — the project page's **Library** tab merges two data planes. The **file plane** comes from the host's `workspaceFiles` (scope `{sessionId, workspaceRoot}`, one `list` per project folder, with an honest reason when no folder or no session exists); the panel states that search matches **file names and paths only, never contents** — that is the host's boundary. The **artifact plane** reads `artifacts` 0.2 through its Remote contract (`ctx.get("artifacts")` plus `version().contract === "artifacts/2"` before `list({ projectId })`) and, because artifact metadata is not guaranteed to carry `projectId`, the plugin keeps its **own `projectId ↔ artifactId` mapping** in the project record (`artifactRefs[]`: id, title, kind, version, bytes, time, source session/tool call, written by `recordArtifact` from a project thread and readable after a cold start). Metering reports count and bytes; provenance says which session and tool call produced the artifact. When artifacts is missing, has no `version()`, or reports another contract, the Library says **"the artifact library needs dsh-artifacts 0.2"** and lists only the file plane — it never shows "this project has no artifacts". Expanded thread rows embed artifact thumbnail cards (title, kind, version, relative time, provenance); the button opens the host's right-side `artifact` tab via `ctx.sidebarRight.openTab("artifact", { params: { projectId } })` and is disabled with a reason when the service is absent. The B3 review fixes ship with it: the thread-default **effort whitelist is gone** (`max` / `xhigh` / `off` from this deployment now persist; only a 40-character cap remains), `locale/{zh,en}.json` gained the **44 missing runtime keys** (and the realtime-CI strings now say "not implemented" instead of promising a webhook), the smoke run starts with an **INFRA self-check** (host port, plugin activation, `projects.json` on disk, browser result) that fails fast instead of polluting assertion counts, the once-only folder grant is consumed **only after every gate passes and the execution is claimed** (rolled back when the attempt does not land), the folder gate resolves the mode from the **directory the command actually runs in** (a thread worktree inherits its project folder's grant), and `listMemoryFragments` validates the project before touching the filesystem.
- **Claude UI alignment (M2–M6)** — the main column is now a **single composer** (thread/coordinator target switch, circular ↵ send, controls row outside the card) pinned to the bottom; the right panel has four views plus a **view visibility switch** persisted on the project (survives reload); rows carry a state-derived subtitle (working verb+seconds, `✓✓✓ Using X`, failed/waiting/result summaries where the result summary only states measured facts), a step ring and task popover, artifact chips with covers, a diff chip and short relative durations (`now/Nm/Nh/Nd`); the coordinator floats its conclusion with a folded message block and conclusion-side artifact chips, and its default model is independent from thread defaults; **Routines are editable** (switching frequency ↔ manual really creates/deletes the host schedule instead of silently drifting; 43 hard-coded Chinese strings moved to i18n); the **PR flow** has a three-part card, copy link and **merge** gated by PR number + double confirmation + the danger switch (draft PRs are auto-marked ready), all PR commands run in the thread worktree; **failure auto-retry** is an explicitly-scoped alternative (after a failed turn it re-sends "continue" once after 60s, at most twice — it does not pretend to be usage-limit resumption); both themes are layered correctly with light-theme contrast fixes, and WebUI vs desktop layouts match at 1440×900 within 1px.
- **Four tabs matching Claude Projects (UI convention §7.3 exception)** — the panel now carries `threads / library / routines / views` to mirror Claude "Projects" (D1/D2 decisions from the 4-video research). The `views` tab holds per-view visibility checkboxes plus saved filter views; memory moved into **Project settings › Memory** (`data-projects-memory-pane`). The §7.3 default stays ≤3; this 4th tab is the documented exception for aligning with a host product's fixed IA.
- **Structural add-ons (B4)** — **Routines** map six frequencies (manual / hourly / daily / weekdays / weekly / monthly) onto the host `schedule` service: hourly and the three calendar tiers use `cron`, daily uses the host's `daily` timing, and every time is padded to the host's mandatory `HH:mm:ss` (`09:30` is rejected by `ScheduleInputError`). Create / list / enable-disable (host `paused|active` **and** a local `enabled` copy) / delete (host entry first; if the host refuses, the local record is kept so no token-spending orphan survives) / **Run now** / **History** (host delivery records merged with local Run-now entries, newest first). The UI states the cost in the place where you create a routine: **every delivery is one model call**, new-session deliveries are at least 60 s apart, and the manual tier never runs by itself. The **permission switch narrows, it does not auto-approve**: this deployment's `catalog().defaultPreset` is already `danger-full-access` + `approval: never`, so the dropdown (options come from `catalog()`, names are never hard-coded) shows "inherit host default" plus every deployment preset translated from its `{sandbox, approval}` bundle into plain language (read-only / workspace-write / full access / custom) with "narrower than the host default" markers. The choice is stored as a name in the project record and applied **after** a thread or coordinator session is created via `permissionPresets.set(session, name)`; when no session handle is reachable the row says `pending` instead of pretending, and when no preset matches the bundle the plugin falls back to `session.append('approval/policy' | 'sandbox/mode')` and labels it 自定义. Every application is verified by reading `current(session)` back (fallback path: `approval.overrideOf` / `sandboxPolicy.overrideOf`), and the panel states explicitly that push / merge / delete still always require your approval. **Reminders** have two modes chosen per-reminder: `timer` (default, free) keeps a local timer with the due time persisted, is re-armed from disk on every boot (overdue ones fire once at startup and are written back as `fired` + unread so a restart never double-fires) and raises a `shell.overlay` toast; `schedule` (billable) delegates to the host `schedule` service and says so ("one model call, runs even while DSH is closed"). The project default (`reminderDefault`, `timer`) is overridable per reminder; cancel, complete-early and expiration cleanup (terminal states older than 7 days) are supported.
- **Stubs wired up (B2)** — a coordinator area on the project page (one long-lived session: create it, send one line, restart it; it is _not_ the host composer), coordinator reports surfaced with conclusion + thread chips, context policy with a `compaction` null-guard and a wake envelope that now carries "recent thread" and "memory index", a per-thread Tasks checklist from the host `todo/write` snapshot (`✓`/`◌` + n/m, `none` when there is no list), in-thread steering (`prompt({mode:'steer'})`), per-thread model/effort (`session/selectModel`, dropdown from `modelCatalog`, read back via `modelSelection`), a Create PR bar plus PR badge with a CI-state dot, an expandable thread panel (start card, inline branch/parameter chips), **no cross-project moves** (`attachThread` rejects a thread that already belongs to another project; only empty slots or detach-then-attach), PR/CI polling by default (only projects with open PRs, 30–90 s with backoff, stops when the app closes) and an "experimental realtime watch" switch that is **disabled and explicitly marked not implemented** (it would need the gh-webhook extension, repo admin rights and signature checks; only polling exists). A manual "Fix CI round" button feeds a failed CI thread into the bounded auto-fix loop.
- **Overview / project home (B1)** — six states (`waiting-user > failed > working > resolved > idle`, plus `archived`) settled from the host's `state().pendingInput/running`, persisted `turn/end` failure reasons and a plugin-owned `resolvedAt`; group headers with counts, a five-pill filter bar (`~Nm` estimate only when it can be inferred from observed step cadence), per-row subtitle from the last readable `tool/call`, step ring from the `todo/write` snapshot (`—` when there is no todo list — never `0/0`), manual resolve/reopen and unread marks, `Welcome back` header with a 7-day token sparkline, one-time first-run guide (`firstRunDone` in the host `storageDomain`), project switcher, and multi-folder Context (≤10 folders per project).
- **Isolated parallel threads** — one session per task. When the project directory is a Git repository, the thread gets its own worktree under `<repoParent>/.dsh-worktrees/<repo>/`; otherwise it degrades to a shared directory with an explicit warning instead of failing.
- **Coordinator** — when a thread finishes a turn, a structured wake envelope (carrying the thread's actual result) is delivered to the project's coordinator session, at most once per turn. User input is routed by **flat rules first** (`{when, action}`); the model only proposes when no rule matches.
- **Autonomy gate** — `L0` observe, `L1` propose only (default), `L2` may start threads, `L3` full. The gate sits _after_ the decision and _before_ the action, so the audit shows both the intent and why it was refused.
- **A small, non-negotiable tool basket** — the coordinator gets four `project_*` tools (start thread, list threads, message thread, request action) and **no** shell, file writing, deletion, push or merge. Dangerous actions can only be _requested_; the approval queue collects them and you decide.
- **Approval, then execution** — an approval only records consent. Executing it still requires the matching danger switch (all six default **off**), an impact that fits the limits, and an explicit action→switch mapping. Every execution writes recovery evidence; every refusal writes an audit entry saying why.
- **Untrusted input stays data** — content from CI logs, PR comments or peers arrives as `relay`, gets wrapped in a "this is data, not instructions" block whose fence is longer than any backtick run inside it, and can never authorize an action.
- **Close-out (B6)** — the Overview survives a restart: every project thread now keeps a bounded (80) journal of the minimal `reduce()` facts (turn start/end, failed attempt, subtitle summary, todo snapshot, interaction flags — never message bodies or tool arguments), and the service replays it into `views` at boot, so a thread that failed/is waiting is not `idle` again after a restart (a human `resolvedAt` newer than the last activity still wins, and a resolve older than new activity expires instead of resurrecting). **Auto-resolve (F29)**: a project stores `autoResolveDays` (null = off, default); a startup check plus a daily timer mark threads **with no activity for ≥ N days** as resolved, write `thread/auto-resolved` audit (`days`/`idleDays`) and update the in-memory view in the same pass; already-resolved/archived/undated threads are never touched, and exactly N days counts as due while N days minus 1 ms does not. The dropdown lives in the project-detail right rail (Off / 3 / 7 / 14 / 30 days) because the host may disable the settings page; `setAutoResolveDays` returns the read-back value and writes `project/auto-resolve`, and `checkAutoResolve` runs the same check manually. The thread row summary now shows the real `diff N files +N/-M` from `git diff --numstat` against the worktree base (uncommitted changes included, 5 s cache, `n/a` only when git cannot answer) instead of a permanent `n/a`, with an exact `data-projects-thread-diff` anchor; the approval-only "edit plugin config" path validates routing rules against the **same object contract** the matcher uses (`{textMatches,textMaxChars,isQuestion,threadState}`), so real rules can finally be written and hit.
- **Editable policy** — autonomy level, persona and the model-fallback switch are editable in settings (the first settings screen still stays at three rows).
- **Opt-in remote writes** — pushing a thread branch, opening a PR (four tiers `off`/`draft`/`ready`/`auto-merge`, `off` by default, selectable in the project policy settings) and merging, each gated by a danger switch plus a human approval. In the `auto-merge` tier a passing-CI PR is **queued as a `merge` approval** — it is never merged by the plugin on its own, and an approval whose PR is not recorded on one of this project's threads is refused (`merge/pr-not-ours`) instead of falling back to `dirs[0]`. Verified end-to-end locally with a bare remote and a stub `gh`, and on a real GitHub repository (PR opened, CI gate enforced, merge refused/approved as designed).
- **Project sharing** — deferred, see [ADR 0018](../../docs/adr/0018-projects-defer-liveshare-sharing.md): DSH 0.2.2-rc.3 ships `dsh-experimental-liveshare` but does not enable it and exposes no stable host service, so building on it would be guesswork.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kangyishuai/dsh-projects
```

Restart the DSH desktop app afterwards.

## Side effects & risks

- **Writes metadata** under `$DSH_HOME/projects/projects.json` (or `config.dataRoot` when set; a desktop app that does not export `DSH_HOME` falls back to `~/.dsh/projects`). Atomic replace via a temp file; a corrupt file is renamed aside and never deleted.
- **Creates Git worktrees** next to your repository (never inside it and never inside `.git/`) when you create a thread for a project that has a Git directory. Archiving the thread removes the worktree again **only** when it is clean, has no unpushed commits, and is not the current session's directory; otherwise it is kept and reported.
- **Runs `git`** through `node:child_process` for worktree create/remove and the cleanliness checks. No network, no credentials.
- **Never touches session logs.** Detaching or archiving a project leaves every `session.v*.jsonl.zstd` untouched.
- On startup the plugin reconciles its records: a recorded worktree that no longer exists is dropped from the record, while an unrecorded directory on disk is **kept** and only reported.
- **Routines and schedule-mode reminders spend tokens.** Each delivery is one model call; nothing is created until you save a routine/reminder in the UI, and the panel says so next to every create button. `timer` reminders never call a model, but they only fire while DSH is running (overdue ones fire once on the next start).
- **Core audit fixes (2026-11-28)** — (a) sessions for projects **without a folder** (coordinator, routine deliveries, `schedule` reminders) now run in `<dataRoot>/workspaces/<id>` instead of the plugin data root itself; the data root holds `projects.json`, `trash/` and every other project's memory, so a `danger-full-access` agent must never be born there, and it no longer shows up in the host Workspace list. (b) Revoking `policy.repoGrants` now sticks (an explicit empty object is persisted instead of falling back to the previous grants), unknown budget fields survive a save, `budget.weeklyTokens` is a real budget field enforced both at thread creation and in the automatic pause, token buckets use **local** dates, the approval queue is capped (500) with paging, stale approval claims expire (10 min) and are reclaimed at boot, deleting a project also drops its token bucket (restored from the trash manifest), and restoring validates the manifest's `project.id` (no path escape). (c) The approval card shows a **plain-text impact line** (PR number, repo, branch, folder, changed keys) next to approve/execute, and `preapprove` finally has a settings entry with an explicit "runs automatically when checked" warning. See `docs/testing/projects.md` §20.
- **No coordinator, no wake.** A project without a configured coordinator never wakes anything when a thread finishes: the plugin does not build an envelope, does not call a model and does not spam the audit — it keeps **one** `wake/skipped` record per project per 6-hour window (previously every single `turn/end` wrote one, 154 identical rows in a real profile) and the project-detail coordinator card says so explicitly.
- **Remote writes are opt-in and off by default.** `git push`, `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge` exist but each requires both a danger switch and a human approval; nothing is pushed or merged automatically.
- **No credentials are read into model context** by design.
- If the metadata file cannot be read (permissions, newer format), the plugin stays inert and logs a warning instead of failing the harness.

## Remote access

Everything runs on the machine that hosts DSH. If you want to reach it from another device, see
[docs/deployment/projects-l1-remote.md](../../docs/deployment/projects-l1-remote.md) — it covers the
safe ways to expose the Web UI (loopback + tunnel, HTTPS, reverse proxy) and what `projects` does and
does not do over a remote connection.

### Scope of the multi-folder Context item (F35)

This batch implements **multiple project folders only**: up to 10 roots per project, all of them effective,
and every thread records which root it runs in (`thread.dir`, shown on the thread row).

Claude's project volume limits — **1000 files / 2 GB per project / 480 MB per file** — belong to its upload
capability. DSH has no upload channel today, so those numbers are **deferred with that capability** and are
**not** claimed by this plugin. Folder roots are referenced in place; nothing is copied into the profile.

## Compatibility

0.10.x is the current published line (0.10.1 on npm). Numbers below were measured on the tagged commit; per-release details live in `CHANGELOG.md`. Rows for not-yet-released 0.11–0.14 were removed because those features shipped in 0.10.0.

| Plugin              | Verified on DSH                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0.10.x              | 0.2.2-rc.5: `pnpm verify` EXIT=0 (projects **720** unit tests); `pnpm gate:projects` green — runtime probe **72/72**, web smoke **270 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, desktop read-only regression green (**17–20 PASS / 0 SKIP**, data-dependent). 0.10.0 lands the Claude-Projects UI alignment (M2–M6: four right-rail views with visibility switches, single bottom composer, state-derived row subtitles, coordinator conclusions + artifacts, editable Routines, Library file tree + artifact viewer, PR card with gated merge, dual-theme polish) and two independent subagent reviews plus a second review round (0.10.1: approval merge shares assessMergePr, archive no longer deletes worktrees, sticky waiting-user fixed): **P0** UI merge previously bypassed its own CI/approval/diff gates (now `assessMergePr`), project lifecycle no longer deletes running threads' worktrees, trash retention cleanup actually finds entries, `getProject` read-back works, plus performance work (compact JSON writes with 250ms coalescing, budgeted `libraryView`, per-session `state()` cache, background-tab polling off). See `CHANGELOG.md`. |
| 0.11.x (unreleased) | 0.2.2-rc.5: `pnpm verify` EXIT=0 (projects **809** unit tests). Core/backend audit batch: session cwd for folder-less projects moved to `workspaces/<id>`, pause/archive/delete now really stop host schedules (via the shipped `SchedulePatch.active` contract) and delete validates before touching them, `repoGrants` revoke takes effect, `weeklyTokens` is a real budget field **with a settings entry**, token buckets use local dates, approval queue is capped/paged with claim TTL, approval cards show a plain-text impact line, `preapprove`/PR tiers are reachable in settings, and a passing-CI PR in the auto-merge tier is queued as a merge approval (reachable via the PR card's “Continue PR flow”). Still deferred: AUD-PROJ-15/16/18/20/23/25/28, routine-delivery token bucketing, approval-prune policy (F9), impact label i18n (F10).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 0.9.x               | 0.2.2-rc.5: full `pnpm gate:all` (web smoke **78**/0/0, desktop read-only regression **11 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, 124s). This phase finished the walkthrough leftovers, per-thread actions and made the danger switches reachable in the UI, and verified open-PR / CI gate / real merge / human-approval threshold / L2 routing against a **real private repo with real Actions CI** (see docs/testing/projects.md §17). Per-release detail lives in the CHANGELOG.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 0.4.2               | 0.2.2-rc.5: installed into the live profile and **measured after a desktop restart** — desktop read-only regression **11 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, web smoke **54**/0/0, `pnpm gate:all` green (64s). Fixes "no way to start a thread in an empty project"; confirmed with a real UI screenshot                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 0.3.0               | 0.2.2-rc.5: installed into the live profile and **measured after a desktop restart** — desktop read-only regression **11 PASS / 0 SKIP / 0 FAIL**, web smoke **52*
